original_text: Universal Model Picker
active_text: Universal Model Picker

original_text:
The Universal Model Picker is the single shared model/provider selection and routing interface for the 9to1 ecosystem. On Windows/regular 9to1 it is hosted by Home; on 9to1-OS the same canonical state is surfaced by the OS. Apps, Agents and AI surfaces MUST NOT create incompatible private model pickers, provider registries or fallback logic when this shared capability applies.
Compact picker and full manager
The compact picker is used inside apps, Agents and AI surfaces when selecting the effective model/route. The full manager lives in Home/Settings → AI/Models and adds provider configuration, installation/acquisition, aliases, defaults, route ordering, background routing, fallbacks, privacy, resource and lifecycle controls.
Entries expose stable Dulche model identity plus user-facing name/alias, provider/source, local/cloud/remote state, modalities/capabilities, tool/structured-output support, reasoning controls, context/output limits, loading/availability, privacy/residency, entitlement/cost where known and local RAM/VRAM fit where meaningful. Display names are never used as canonical identity.
Simple defaults and capability categories
The normal picker keeps the primary capability configuration approachable: Chat Model/Route, Image Model/Route and Voice Model/Voice. Advanced exposes Audio Model/Route and Video Model/Route. The user may instead choose one Active Model/Route and allow all compatible capabilities to inherit it, with ordered fallback resolving unsupported capabilities.
Chat is the primary general-purpose route for conversation, reasoning, writing, coding, tool use, agentic work and multimodal chat where supported.
Image supports an explicit Inherit from Active/Chat route. Inheritance means use that ordered route and its native image-generation/editing-capable candidates; it MUST NOT silently substitute an unrelated unconfigured image provider. A dedicated Image route is an explicit override.
Voice is the first-class conversational/live-voice selection used by Vision & Voice for supported Conversational, Monologue, Live Listener and Live Translate modes. When the selected Voice Model exposes named voices, the user-facing field is labelled Voice and selects VoiceID while showing VoiceModelID as secondary metadata. When there are no named variants the field remains Voice Model.
Advanced Audio covers dedicated transcription, synthesis, audio understanding/transformation or music/audio generation where applicable. Advanced Video covers video generation, editing/transformation or video-native understanding. These category routes may inherit the Active route or use explicit independent ordered routes.
Active and Background routes
Users may configure a single Active Model/Route for all foreground AI work or assign capability-specific/app/Agent overrides. Separately, a Background Model/Route can be configured for non-interactive work such as background summarisation, indexing/classification, Background Learning processing, permitted Automations AI work, proactive suggestions and other low-priority background tasks.
If no Background route is configured, background work inherits the Active route subject to normal capability/privacy/policy filtering. A task-specific explicit model outranks Agent/app/category defaults; a configured Background route applies only to eligible background work and MUST NOT override an explicit Agent/task requirement.
Ordered Model Routes
Home/Dulche MUST support versioned ordered Model Routes shared by regular 9to1 and 9to1-OS. A Model Route is an ordered list of stable configured model identities plus per-entry enabled/disabled state and routing policy. Users can reorder candidates directly in Home, including by drag/reorder UI, without changing the models' canonical identities.
Example: an Active route may be ChatGPT 6 Sol → Gemma 4 → Fable 5. The ordering means use the highest-priority candidate that is both eligible and available for the request. The router MUST evaluate compatibility before invocation rather than deliberately sending impossible requests to higher entries first.
Foreground and background workloads may use different ordered routes. A user can therefore choose a powerful cloud model first for interactive work while using a small local model first for background work. Users who want simplicity can select a single model and leave fallback entries empty.
Eligibility-first routing
For every routed request Dulche first derives task requirements such as modality/capability, tool use, structured output, context/output requirements, reasoning support and foreground/background role. It then filters candidates against provider/model capability, privacy/locality policy, administrator policy, connection/authentication permission, user fallback policy, entitlement and other hard constraints before considering route priority.
After filtering, Dulche selects the highest-priority available candidate. A lower candidate may be used automatically when a higher candidate is unavailable because of a classified routing condition such as usage/quota exhaustion, provider/model outage, unsupported required capability, context incompatibility, authentication/provider unavailability when another authorised option exists, or local resource insufficiency after permitted reclamation.
Capability mismatch should normally be detected before invocation. For example, if the first two models in a route cannot generate video and the third can, a video-generation request routes directly to the third eligible model rather than failing through the first two.
Conditions that are not model fallback
Model fallback is not a generic retry mechanism. Errors such as missing user files, invalid tool arguments, target-app permission denial, required human approval, business-logic rejection or an external service action failure do not justify silently switching models unless the failure is independently classified as a model/provider-routing condition.
Fallback privacy and control
Each route and candidate can restrict fallback, including no fallback, local-only fallback, cloud-allowed fallback or provider-specific constraints. A route containing cloud candidates does not itself authorise sensitive context to leave the device. Privacy, administrator and task policies are evaluated before route ordering.
A request explicitly pinned to a model with fallback disabled MUST fail transparently rather than silently substitute another model. Likewise a local-only request cannot fall through to cloud merely because the local model is unavailable.
Routing transparency
The effective model and routing reason remain inspectable. Home/Dulche records route identity, selected model and skipped/fallback reasons where relevant, for example 'Sol skipped: usage exhausted; Gemma selected' or 'Sol skipped: video-generation unsupported; Fable selected'. This metadata may be surfaced subtly in normal UI and in more detail through diagnostics/Action Graph without cluttering every response.
Selection inheritance and overrides
The configuration hierarchy MUST be deterministic: request-specific explicit selection → Agent/task override → app/surface override → capability/category route → Background route for eligible background work or Active route for foreground work → configured route fallbacks. A lower-level explicit override wins, while inherited state is visibly distinguishable from an explicit override.
LLM Space and Desktop Space overrides MAY exist but remain scoped. Category overrides are independent; for example an LLM Space may override Chat while inheriting global Image/Voice/Audio/Video routes.
Reasoning and capability validation
The picker renders only reasoning/effort levels actually exposed by the selected model/provider. It MUST NOT invent Low/Medium/High controls for a model that does not support them. Incompatible explicit selections are blocked or clearly explained unless an authorised fallback route can satisfy the requirement.
Aliases and model identity
Users can assign friendly aliases/nicknames to models. Aliases are presentation conveniences and may be duplicated; all routing objects store stable provider-scoped Dulche ModelID values so duplicate names never create ambiguous execution.
Local model lifecycle
Where supported, the full manager provides discover/install or pull, import, verify, download progress, load, unload, remove, update/replace, rollback, storage-location and compatible CPU/GPU/offload configuration. These operations use Dulche Runtime/Den and provider/package APIs rather than a second model-host implementation.
Provider support
Routes may contain compatible local runtimes, configured commercial/cloud providers, self-hosted/OpenAI-compatible endpoints, Ollama, another Dulche device, enterprise endpoints and authorised provider/Plugin implementations. Provider authentication and credentials remain owned by the appropriate shared credential/provider system.
Resource awareness
For local candidates the picker may show estimated RAM/VRAM requirement, current availability, loading state and reclaimable resources when known. On 9to1-OS this integrates with the AI-aware resource manager; on other Home platforms it uses the available Dulche/runtime resource information without pretending OS-level reclamation exists where it does not.
Administrator and managed-profile policy
Managed profiles may limit approved models/providers, acquisition, external cloud use, maximum cost/usage class or fallback destinations. Policy filtering happens before user ordering so reordering a blocked provider cannot bypass a School/organisation restriction.
Universal Model Picker acceptance requirements
* Regular 9to1/Home and 9to1-OS use one canonical Dulche model catalogue and versioned routing contract.
* Users can use one Active Model for everything compatible or configure separate capability/app/Agent and Background routes.
* Ordered model routing automatically falls through on classified quota, availability, capability, context or resource conditions while respecting privacy, permissions and admin policy.
* Capability mismatch is filtered before invocation where knowable; model fallback is not misused for unrelated tool/app/business-logic failures.
* Users can reorder, enable/disable and inspect route candidates and understand which model ultimately handled a request.

Errors such as missing user files, invalid tool arguments, target-app permission denial, required human approval, business-logic rejection or an external service action failure do not justify silently switching models unless the failure is independently classified as a model/provider-routing condition.
Fallback privacy and control
Each route and candidate can restrict fallback, including no fallback, local-only fallback, cloud-allowed fallback or provider-specific constraints. A route containing cloud candidates does not itself authorise sensitive context to leave the device. Privacy, administrator and task policies are evaluated before route ordering.
A request explicitly pinned to a model with fallback disabled MUST fail transparently rather than silently substitute another model. Likewise a local-only request cannot fall through to cloud merely because the local model is unavailable.
Routing transparency
The effective model and routing reason remain inspectable. Home/Dulche records route identity, selected model and skipped/fallback reasons where relevant, for example 'Sol skipped: usage exhausted; Gemma selected' or 'Sol skipped: video-generation unsupported; Fable selected'. This metadata may be surfaced subtly in normal UI and in more detail through diagnostics/Action Graph without cluttering every response.
Selection inheritance and overrides
The configuration hierarchy MUST be deterministic: request-specific explicit selection → Agent/task override → app/surface override → capability/category route → Background route for eligible background work or Active route for foreground work → configured route fallbacks. A lower-level explicit override wins, while inherited state is visibly distinguishable from an explicit override.
LLM Space and Desktop Space overrides MAY exist but remain scoped. Category overrides are independent; for example an LLM Space may override Chat while inheriting global Image/Voice/Audio/Video routes.
Reasoning and capability validation
The picker renders only reasoning/effort levels actually exposed by the selected model/provider. It MUST NOT invent Low/Medium/High controls for a model that does not support them. Incompatible explicit selections are blocked or clearly explained unless an authorised fallback route can satisfy the requirement.
Aliases and model identity
Users can assign friendly aliases/nicknames to models. Aliases are presentation conveniences and may be duplicated; all routing objects store stable provider-scoped Dulche ModelID values so duplicate names never create ambiguous execution.
Local model lifecycle
Where supported, the full manager provides discover/install or pull, import, verify, download progress, load, unload, remove, update/replace, rollback, storage-location and compatible CPU/GPU/offload configuration. These operations use Dulche Runtime/Den and provider/package APIs rather than a second model-host implementation.
Provider support
Routes may contain compatible local runtimes, configured commercial/cloud providers, self-hosted/OpenAI-compatible endpoints, Ollama, another Dulche device, enterprise endpoints and authorised provider/Plugin implementations. Provider authentication and credentials remain owned by the appropriate shared credential/provider system.
Resource awareness
For local candidates the picker may show estimated RAM/VRAM requirement, current availability, loading state and reclaimable resources when known. On 9to1-OS this integrates with the AI-aware resource manager; on other Home platforms it uses the available Dulche/runtime resource information without pretending OS-level reclamation exists where it does not.
Administrator and managed-profile policy
Managed profiles may limit approved models/providers, acquisition, external cloud use, maximum cost/usage class or fallback destinations. Policy filtering happens before user ordering so reordering a blocked provider cannot bypass a School/organisation restriction.
Universal Model Picker acceptance requirements
* Regular 9to1/Home and 9to1-OS use one canonical Dulche model catalogue and versioned routing contract.
* Users can use one Active Model for everything compatible or configure separate capability/app/Agent and Background routes.
* Ordered model routing automatically falls through on classified quota, availability, capability, context or resource conditions while respecting privacy, permissions and admin policy.
* Capability mismatch is filtered before invocation where knowable; model fallback is not misused for unrelated tool/app/business-logic failures.
* Users can reorder, enable/disable and inspect route candidates and understand which model ultimately handled a request.

original_text:
Floating compose @ invocation menu
The shared Home-owned floating AI compose component MUST provide one searchable @ invocation menu for Plugins, Skills, Apps, Agents and Files. The menu is a single interaction surface with collapsible type sections rather than separate unrelated pickers. Typing @ opens the resource list; typing text after @ filters across all sections while preserving each result's type and identity.
Selecting an item inserts an inline invocation chip/token inside the compose field at the caret position. The rendered token MUST display the resource's icon where available plus its human-readable label, for example an Agent may render as '@[agent icon] John'. The token MUST use a distinct invoked visual state, including colour/style differentiation, while also using non-colour cues for accessibility. Editing/deleting the token removes or changes the invocation rather than leaving invisible hidden attachment state.
Invocation tokens MUST store stable canonical identities, not only display text: Plugin PackageID/version or resolved active version, SkillID/version, AppID, AgentID/DefinitionRevision where required and File/Artifact reference identity/revision or access token as appropriate. Duplicate display names MUST therefore remain unambiguous. The resolved invocation set is included in request metadata, FullLog and Action Graph.
The Plugins section lists Dulche Plugins enabled/available in the current scope; Skills lists eligible Dulche Skills including the built-in Persistent Skill; Agents lists Agents available through Dulche scope resolution; Files searches authorised files/artifacts without silently granting new access. Availability in the picker never grants permission to execute protected actions or read inaccessible content.
The Apps section MUST contain every installed/available first-party 9to1 app plus user-installed applications that 9to1 can classify as safely operable through a typed API/integration or, when separately authorised, Computer Use. App entries MUST expose whether their interaction path is Typed/API, Computer Use Required, or both. Selecting an app whose only route is Computer Use MUST NOT activate Computer Use by itself; the request also requires the explicit @Computer Use invocation.
Game executables and anti-cheat-protected game surfaces MUST be excluded from the operable Apps invocation results even when discovered through Steam, Epic Games Launcher or another launcher/library. If 9to1 cannot confidently distinguish an eligible ordinary application from a game/anti-cheat target, it MUST omit or mark the target unavailable for Computer Use rather than risk automation. Play remains the supported Agent-game route defined by its own contract.
@Computer Use is a reserved first-party system capability entry in the same searchable invocation surface. Selecting it creates the explicit ComputerUseInvocationID required by the Dulche Computer Use contract and makes its active state visible in the compose field before the request is submitted.
Cross-app execution visualisation
Models operating inside any 9to1 app MAY invoke another 9to1 app only when the user's request explicitly names/invokes that app, directly asks for an outcome owned by that app, or unambiguously implies the owning app from the requested artifact/action. For example, 'create a presentation' resolves to Present; 'make a spreadsheet' resolves to Data; an unrelated app MUST NOT be opened merely because the model thinks it might be useful.
Cross-app intent resolution MUST bind to the owning app's stable AppID and typed capability contract. If the required app is not running, Home MAY launch/open it automatically when that is part of fulfilling the request. The target artifact remains canonical in its owning app, and the originating app/Space receives references/status rather than an unmanaged duplicate.
Typed app APIs and shared semantic actions are the normal execution path. Computer Use is not a fallback for missing/failed APIs and remains unavailable unless @Computer Use was explicitly invoked. Permission, review, edit/suggest/view state, conflicts and external-side-effect rules of the target app still apply to cross-app work.
Where an app has a visible editing surface, the user SHOULD be able to watch model-driven edits occur in real time. Home/shared app infrastructure MUST provide an execution-visualisation stream that maps semantic actions to visible UI changes such as objects moving, text appearing, selections changing, slides being created or a virtual cursor hovering over the affected target.
The execution visualiser is representational, not the control mechanism. A virtual cursor MUST be visually distinguishable from the user's real pointer and MUST NOT generate mouse/keyboard input merely to make the animation believable. The canonical typed API/action result remains authoritative; visual animation follows confirmed/provisional semantic events and MUST reconcile to final app state after errors, retries or rollback.
AI conversation presentation settings
Home Settings MUST expose global conversation presentation preferences for Plain text versus Speech bubbles. The preference applies to compatible 9to1 conversational/AI surfaces through the shared renderer rather than each app inventing a different message layout.
User-message alignment and model-message alignment MUST be independently configurable as Left or Right. All four combinations are valid, including both parties on the same side. Alignment changes presentation only and MUST NOT alter message order, authorship, accessibility reading order or exported conversation data.
The selected Dulche thinking-log mode (Precise, Concise, Detailed or Ramble) MUST be configurable in the same AI/conversation settings family. Inline thinking/work regions render beneath or between message text according to chronology; when Speech bubbles are enabled, the thinking/work region visually belongs beneath the relevant model bubble without being styled as ordinary model-authored message text.
Thinking/work presentation MUST use lower visual emphasis than normal chat while remaining readable and accessible. Collapsed 'Thought for ...'/'Worked for ...', ETA status, blockers and Problem events MUST use the same shared renderer across apps so equivalent Runtime state is not represented differently by each product.

original_text: Acceptance requirements
active_text: Acceptance requirements

original_text:
Home is implementation-complete only when acceptance coverage verifies at least:
* A native app refuses normal startup when Home is not installed and successfully resumes through the trusted Install Home/bootstrap flow.
* Closing the visible Home window does not break dependent apps while Home Core remains healthy.
* A Home Core/service crash produces structured degraded state in attached apps, preserves user artifacts and reconnects after service recovery without spawning duplicate private services.
* Dashboard manual tile add/remove/resize/reorder/pin state persists across restart and responsive window sizes.
* AllowAIGeneratedTiles=false prevents arbitrary generated tile creation while existing tiles continue to function.
* AllowAIReorder=false prevents AI movement/layout changes; when enabled, AI cannot move pinned/locked tiles and every AI layout change is reversible.
* Generated Dashboard tiles expose source provenance and fail stale/unavailable rather than fabricating live data.
* Apps install/update/repair/rollback uses the shared package database and survives a failed staged activation without deleting user artifacts.
* Library opens the same canonical artifact in its owning app rather than creating a duplicate.
* Events preserve typed source records and link to the corresponding Action Graph/entity where applicable.
* Discover aggregates at least two configured model/provider sources without identity collisions and performs a valid install/connect action.
* Universal Model Picker override precedence and fallback policy resolve deterministically and do not cross local-to-cloud boundaries when policy forbids it.
* Permission/trust grants can be inspected, narrowed/revoked/blocked and future calls immediately respect the updated state.
* Mesh pairing establishes stable device identity; capability calls obey both ends’ permissions; device revocation prevents subsequent sync/invocation.
* Home notifications preserve read/dismiss state and typed deep links across restart and OS notification bridging.
* Search/Library results stop exposing content after permission revocation/deletion and indexes can be rebuilt without source-data loss.
* A representative shared productivity object can round-trip across Write, Present, Canvas, Boards and Spaces through the Shared Productivity Engine without schema/format loss.
* Account/subscription values shown in Home match the server-authoritative CAKE ID entitlement state and are not inferred from preset labels.
* An app with an incompatible required Home service version is blocked into update/repair instead of running against an undefined interface.
* Home persistent control-plane state can recover from process interruption without silently dropping package activation state, device trust or permission grants.

original_text:
9to1 Admin
ADM-01 — Product role, access and platforms
9to1 Admin is a standalone Business-exclusive 9to1 application, not a renamed account-settings page or WordPress administration screen. It is the organisation-management interface for the Business features specified separately under Business features — functional specification. Business and Business + include it; the account-bound free Business grant defined for Jacob also applies. App access does not grant administrative permissions: every operation additionally requires the appropriate role and target scope.
Admin MUST have Windows, 9to1-OS and browser/web surfaces sharing the same CAKE ID, organisation entities, domain APIs and permission evaluation. Native clients use Home’s shared services. The web app uses authenticated shared web services without requiring a local Home installation for ordinary organisation administration. Device operations require an enrolled compatible endpoint; a browser cannot directly enforce unsupported local OS controls. Unsupported capabilities MUST remain distinguishable from denied permission or an offline device.
Admin owns management workflows and policy editing. The account/billing service owns subscriptions and ledgers; Spaces owns Team Spaces; Files owns shared-drive content; Connect owns communications; Home/Mesh owns pairing and device-resource execution; Dulche/Den owns Agents; the 9to1-OS policy service owns endpoint enforcement. Admin MUST invoke these canonical services rather than create duplicate content, Agent registries, payment records or a competing permission broker. This is a native CUI product built on those existing services; no new paid administration donor or hosting service is selected by this specification.
ADM-02 — Navigation and organisation lifecycle
The start screen MUST list organisations the user can manage, with an explicit organisation switcher and current organisation identity on every administrative screen. Navigation MUST include Overview; People; Roles & Permissions; Policies; Models, Apps & Features; Plugins & Settings; Usage & Credits; Billing; Team Space & Drive; Connect; Devices & Mesh; Team Agents; and Audit & Activity. Visibility is permission-filtered, while denial states explain the required capability without leaking inaccessible organisations.
Overview MUST show member/seat counts, resource allocation and consumption, pending invitations/approvals, policy-deployment status, blocked actions, device health and billing state, each with source freshness. Unknown or stale values MUST NOT appear as zero or healthy. Search, filtering, accessible keyboard operation, bulk-selection previews and per-item bulk results are required. Admin is not an artifact editor: blank-document/template import surfaces are not applicable; organisation creation, invitation and configuration import/export replace them.
Authorised owners MUST be able to create and edit organisation identity, manage ownership, inspect linked Business entitlement, archive/reactivate the organisation and request export or deletion. Ownership transfer requires authenticated acceptance by the recipient; removing or suspending the last active owner MUST be rejected. Archive is recoverable and distinct from permanent deletion. Deletion requires an impact preview, explicit confirmation and the applicable retention/export workflow, and MUST NOT delete a member’s personal account or personal artifacts.
ADM-03 — People, roles and permissions
People management MUST support invite, resend/revoke invitation, accept, list/search, assign/change roles, suspend, reinstate and remove membership. Membership states MUST distinguish Invited, Active, Suspended and Removed, with stable MembershipID and UserID. Invitations are time-bounded and single-use for the intended identity. Acceptance and capacity reservation MUST be transactional so concurrent requests cannot bypass the seat cap. The UI MUST distinguish members, pending/reserved invitations and external Connect correspondents; corresponding counting rules must be explicit, not hidden billing assumptions.
Roles MUST be editable capability sets, not just labels. Provide owner, administrator and member roles, plus separately assignable billing, usage-reporting, device-management, Agent-management and audit-reading capabilities. Custom roles MUST support scoped read, add/edit, delete/recovery and specialised administrative actions. A role editor MUST show effective permissions and inherited restrictions. A delegated administrator MUST NOT grant capabilities outside their own delegation boundary, elevate themselves to owner or modify protected grants. Membership alone does not grant access to every shared document, private conversation or Agent memory.
Suspension/removal MUST revoke organisation sessions/capabilities, block new organisation-funded jobs, remove applicable shared access and reconcile owned organisation resources and outstanding reservations. Show a transfer/reassignment preview for shared assets, scheduled Automations and Agent responsibilities. Already completed external actions remain historical facts. Revocation MUST leave personal accounts and unrelated organisations intact; offline devices must report pending revocation until enforcement is acknowledged.
ADM-04 — Enforced policy editor
Administrators MUST be able to enforce organisation-wide and role-specific policies, inspect their effective result for a selected member/device/Agent, and preview affected objects before publication. PolicySet and PolicyAssignment records MUST carry stable IDs, schema version, revision, scope, author, effective time and change reason. A change follows Draft → Validated → Published, with per-target delivery/enforcement status; publication is not proof that an offline endpoint applied it.
Restrictions MUST cover model/provider access; apps; individual app features/actions; Plugins and their capabilities; Agents and Automations, including creation, editing, invocation, schedules and external side effects. Restricted capabilities must be enforced by the owning service at dispatch, not merely hidden in the UI. APIs, command-line tools, modified clients and nested Agent/Plugin calls receive the same policy decisions.
Effective capability grants are the intersection of server entitlement, delegated role, organisation/role policy, object access, caller trust and applicable device/privacy restrictions. A denial at a required boundary cannot be overridden by a broader grant elsewhere. Conflicting mandatory settings or required-versus-blocked Plugin rules MUST produce a validation conflict instead of an arbitrary last-write-wins outcome. New sensitive requests remain subject to Home’s normal approval rules.
ADM-05 — Required Plugins, forced settings and default models
Admin MUST support required organisation-wide Plugins and additional requirements by role, with package identity, approved version/update policy, required configuration and deployment status. Required does not mean silently trusted: package integrity, compatibility, requested scopes and secret connections must validate before enablement. A blocked or failed required Plugin produces an actionable non-compliance state. Disabling an unsafe Plugin remains possible for authorised security response; updates cannot widen permissions without the required approval.
Administrators MUST be able to force supported organisation/role settings and separately supply editable defaults. Members see the effective value, whether it is locked and which policy supplies it. Settings must be addressed by versioned typed keys supported by the target app/device; unsupported settings cannot be reported as applied. Forced settings affect only the managed scope and cannot silently rewrite personal settings outside it.
Default-model configuration MUST support organisation defaults and role-specific defaults, plus permitted user overrides. The effective model must also satisfy model restrictions, entitlement, capability, privacy and local/cloud routing rules. An unavailable or prohibited default blocks with a clear reason or uses an explicitly authorised fallback; it MUST NOT silently send private local-only content to a cloud provider. Conflicting forced role defaults must be resolved explicitly in policy configuration before publication.
ADM-06 — Subscription assignment, usage controls and rollover
Usage & Credits MUST let authorised administrators assign a funded subscription/resource configuration to a member or role, choose a shared organisation pool or individually partitioned allocations, set limits, inspect consumption/reservations and move eligible unspent organisation-owned allocation between partitions. Changing a display tier or role MUST NOT mint credits, unlock an unfunded model band or duplicate an allocation. A cost-changing assignment requires the Billing approval flow rather than silently purchasing resources.
Controls MUST include organisation, role and member ceilings for AI usage and applicable storage/site resources; warnings and hard-stop behaviour; configured time windows; and model/Agent/Automation attribution. original_text:
Files is implementation-complete only when acceptance coverage verifies at least:
* The CUI port accounts for applicable Files/WinUI donor functionality and preserves its core layout/workflows/QoL through a donor-parity manifest.
* 9to1 Drive appears as a normal first-class location and the same FileID opened via web and desktop represents the same canonical hosted object.
* Rename/create/move on one connected client appears live on another client without manual refresh and preserves stable item identity.
* Moving/renaming a file while it is open in its owning app does not break the open document because the app remains attached by FileID.
* Manual Sync now flushes eligible pending operations, retrieves server deltas and reports unresolved errors/conflicts.
* A CloudOnly file hydrates on demand; AvailableOffline works without network; AlwaysAvailable survives restart/cache cleanup.
* Free up space refuses to evict unsynced content and verifies durable cloud revision before eviction.
* Offline structural operations survive device restart and reconcile correctly after reconnect.
* Two conflicting concurrent binary/raw-file edits preserve both revisions or create an explicit conflict; no version is silently lost.
* Two collaborators concurrently reorganising the same hierarchy receive deterministic structural conflict behaviour rather than blind last-write-wins.
* A large resumable upload survives Files/Home restart and continues from validated committed progress.
* A failed transfer integrity check is reported as failure and never as completed.
* Version history and restore preserve later history and identify actor/source/revision.
* Trash/restore/purge behave distinctly and purge uses the elevated destructive flow.
* Sharing/ACL changes propagate to connected clients and revocation prevents future authorised access.
* Creating Write/Present/Data/Board/Canvas artifacts from Files invokes the owning app and creates canonical artifacts.
* Create Stack here/from this folder produces the expected Stack project without duplicating existing source.
* Owning-app real-time collaboration commits durable Files revisions without Files attempting semantic content merges.
* Provider capability differences disable/report unsupported operations rather than pretending support.
* Bulk operations return exact succeeded/failed/skipped outcomes and never silently lose items.
* Private local content is not sent to a cloud AI merely because it is selected in Files.
* Change-feed cursor resume does not require a full filesystem rescan and does not duplicate consequential events.
* Home crash/recovery preserves pending sync journal state and does not create duplicate operations or storage corruption.
* A very large hierarchy can process ordinary incremental changes without complete rescans for each event.

original_text:
Connect
Product role and donor strategy
9to1 Connect is the native CUI communications and collaboration application for people, teams and organisations. It combines real-time messaging, voice/video calling, SMS/RCS integration, organisational collaboration and the full Mail experience inside one coherent product. Connect is the parent communications product; Mail remains a first-class child mode/subsystem rather than being removed or flattened into chat.
The whole Connect application MUST use an open-source donor/reference for mature real-time communications behaviour. Element, together with Matrix as its underlying open communications protocol/reference architecture, is the preferred donor/reference for real-time messaging, rooms/conversations, threading, reactions, multi-device state, end-to-end encryption, presence-compatible collaboration and calling. The selected donor revision and applicable licensing obligations MUST be recorded in the donor-parity manifest before implementation.
The existing Mail subsystem retains Thunderbird as its preferred mature donor/reference for email protocol, MIME, IMAP/SMTP, authentication, offline mail, attachments, drafts, folders/labels, threading, certificates and mature email edge cases. Connect MUST NOT replace Thunderbird mail behaviour with a reduced chat-derived email implementation.
Donor parity applies to mature behavioural capability, interoperability and edge-case handling, not donor-native visual chrome. Connect MUST use a modern native CUI design consistent with 9to1. Proprietary donor services or branding MUST be replaced with 9to1-native equivalents where required.
Architecture and canonical entities
Connect MUST maintain stable canonical identities for at least UserID, ProfileID, OrganisationID, MembershipID, RoleID, ConversationID, RoomID/ChannelID where applicable, MessageID, ThreadID, CallID, ParticipantID, ContactRelationshipID, ReportID, IncidentID, EnforcementActionID and BanEvasionCaseID. Display names, usernames, email addresses, phone numbers, room names and mutable paths MUST NOT be used as canonical identity.
Email messages remain Mail entities governed by the Mail subsystem and its provider semantics. Native Connect chat/room messages remain Connect/Matrix-style communication entities. The product MAY provide unified navigation/search/notifications over both, but MUST NOT merge email and real-time messaging into one incompatible storage/protocol model.
Connect SHOULD use canonical 9to1 services rather than duplicating them. Shared files SHOULD reference canonical Files objects when applicable; assignments/tasks SHOULD reference canonical Planner objects where appropriate; Home owns notifications/permissions; Dulche provides AI; Contacts/people services own canonical contact data where defined.
Conversations, organisations and hierarchy
Connect MUST support one-to-one conversations, group conversations, organisation/team rooms or channels, threaded replies, reactions, message edits, message deletion according to policy, typing indicators, read state/receipts where enabled, presence/availability controls, mentions, attachments/media and conversation search subject to encryption/indexing constraints.
Users MAY belong to multiple organisations simultaneously. Organisations MUST support nested teams/departments/groups and explicit role/membership relationships, including organisational hierarchies such as management/employee or school leadership/department/teacher/student structures. Hierarchy MUST be represented through stable role/membership data rather than inferred only from room placement or display names.
Role and organisation policy MAY govern room creation, membership management, announcement rights, moderation powers, task assignment and administrative settings, but organisation policy MUST NOT silently override personal privacy protections that are not genuinely necessary for the organisation to operate.
Mail mode
Mail is a first-class Connect mode and retains the complete canonical Mail specification, Mail APIs and Thunderbird donor contract. Users MUST be able to use Mail as a complete manual email client with AI unavailable. Connect MUST provide coherent navigation between Mail and real-time communications while preserving the different underlying protocols, privacy properties and provider semantics.
Mail MAY remain independently deep-linkable and launchable where the package/shell architecture supports app shortcuts, but such launch targets resolve to the Mail mode of the canonical Connect application rather than creating a second incompatible Mail implementation.
Native messaging encryption and privacy
Native Connect conversations MUST use end-to-end encryption by default. Ordinary native Connect users MUST NOT be offered a misleading normal-chat mode that silently downgrades private communication to server-readable plaintext merely for implementation convenience.
The implementation MUST follow the platform-wide Privacy Ceiling and apply stricter communications protections where required. Content decryption keys MUST be available only to authorised endpoint devices/participants under the declared trust model. Servers MUST NOT possess a universal content-decryption key or silent moderation/decryption backdoor while the product claims E2EE.
Multi-device encryption MUST define device identity, device trust, key distribution, verification, rotation, lost-device handling, session recovery and cryptographic backup/recovery. Recovery MUST NOT introduce a server-held master key that silently allows universal message decryption.
Connect MUST minimise communication metadata separately from content encryption. Participant graphs, timestamps, delivery state, IP/network information, device identifiers, routing metadata and notification data MUST be collected/retained only as required for operation, safety or declared policy and MUST NOT be presented to users as E2EE-protected when they are observable to infrastructure.
Notification delivery MUST minimise plaintext leakage. Notification previews of encrypted conversations MUST use the most private technically reliable path and MUST respect user settings; push providers MUST NOT receive unnecessary message content.
Search/indexing over encrypted content SHOULD occur locally or through another architecture that preserves the declared E2EE model. Server-side plaintext indexing of native E2EE conversations is prohibited unless the user has explicitly exported/disclosed specific content into a separately governed service.
Disappearing messages
Connect MUST support disappearing-message policies at conversation and/or message scope. Policies MAY include predefined and custom expiry periods and MUST expose the active expiry state visibly enough for participants to understand it.
Expiry MUST be represented canonically and reconcile across authorised devices, including devices that were offline at the expiry time. Expired content MUST be removed from ordinary conversation history and applicable local indexes/caches according to the declared lifecycle.
Connect MUST NOT claim that disappearing messages prevent screenshots, manual copying, external capture or information already legitimately disclosed outside the conversation. Quoted/replied-to message representations MUST NOT preserve the full expired content indefinitely unless an explicit retention/evidence rule requires it.
Safety reports/evidence records that lawfully and transparently retain reported content are separate from ordinary disappearing-message history and MUST have their own access, purpose and retention policy.
SMS and RCS
Connect MUST support SMS and RCS where the current platform, telephony stack, carrier/provider and user permissions allow it. SMS/RCS identities and transport state MUST remain distinct from native Connect messaging.
The UI MUST truthfully represent the protection of the actual transport used. Ordinary SMS MUST NOT be labelled end-to-end encrypted. RCS MUST show E2EE only when encryption has actually been negotiated/supported for that conversation and participant set.
If an intended RCS message would fall back to SMS, any material change in privacy/security capability MUST be represented clearly enough that the user is not led to believe the stronger state still applies. Transport fallback MUST NOT reuse an E2EE badge/state from the prior route.
Voice and video calling
Connect MUST provide mature one-to-one and group voice/video calling with expected modern functionality including incoming/outgoing calls, ringing, missed calls, call history, join/leave/reconnect, participant roster, grid/speaker layouts, pin/spotlight where applicable, microphone mute/unmute, camera enable/disable, camera switching, input/output device selection, screen/window/application sharing, optional system-audio sharing where supported, reactions, raise hand, in-call text chat, picture-in-picture/full-screen and accessible keyboard/screen-reader controls.
Calls MUST use end-to-end encrypted media wherever the selected call architecture supports the native Connect trust model. Signalling and sensitive call state SHOULD receive equivalent or stronger protection where technically feasible. Infrastructure MUST NOT claim stronger privacy than the actual transport provides.
Microphone, camera and screen-capture permissions MUST be explicit, visible and revocable. Joining a call MUST NOT silently enable the camera or microphone contrary to the user's saved/default state. The UI MUST continuously and unmistakably show local mic/camera/screen-share state.
Call infrastructure MUST minimise retained metadata, and self-hosted/private infrastructure SHOULD be supported where compatible with the donor/protocol architecture. TURN/relay/direct-connect behaviour and the associated exposure of participant network addresses MUST be documented and privacy-aware.
Background blur, noise suppression, gain control, camera filters/effects, virtual backgrounds and similar media processing SHOULD run locally where technically practical. A cosmetic filter MUST NOT silently upload raw camera/microphone content to an external processor.
Recording, transcription and AI participation
Recording is disabled by default. Starting recording MUST use a Request Recording workflow rather than an immediate unilateral record action.
Before recording begins, every current participant MUST explicitly approve the recording request. Any participant declining or failing to approve within the defined request state prevents recording from starting. Approval is scoped to that recording session and MUST NOT become a permanent blanket permission.
When recording is active, all participants MUST receive a persistent, unmistakable recording indicator. A participant joining after recording has started MUST be informed before/while joining that recording is active and MUST explicitly acknowledge/approve participation under the recording state before their media is included. A new participant's refusal MUST prevent their media from being recorded and, where the architecture cannot isolate them, MUST pause/stop recording until consent is resolved.
Recording state, requester, participant approvals, start/stop times and resulting artifact identity MUST be auditable. Recordings MUST be stored as permissioned canonical artifacts with explicit owner/access/retention policy rather than hidden provider blobs.
Recording permission MUST NOT imply permission for transcription, AI summarisation or remote model processing. Recording, transcription and AI participation are separate capabilities with separate disclosure/permission requirements.
Adding Dulche, an Agent, transcription service or other non-human processor to a human conversation/call MUST be visible to affected participants where it can receive their communication. Ordinary access by the local Connect client to decrypted E2EE content does NOT automatically grant Dulche/cloud models access.
Contact and communication privacy controls
Connect MUST provide first-class Block, Mute and Contact Settings controls. Blocking and muting MUST be semantically distinct: mute suppresses attention/notifications according to user policy; block prevents the blocked identity from contacting/interacting with the blocker through applicable Connect channels and MUST be enforced beyond merely hiding content locally.
Contact Settings MUST allow the user to control, where applicable, who can directly message them, call them, video call them, add/invite them to groups, see presence/last-active, see read receipts and access profile/contact fields. Unknown contacts MAY be routed to message/contact requests rather than the primary inbox.
Per-conversation notification/mute controls, read-receipt controls, presence controls, privacy/discoverability controls and block lists MUST be available without requiring AI.
Reporting and Trust & Safety
Connect MUST provide a first-class Report workflow for inappropriate, abusive, fraudulent or illegal content/behaviour. Reporting MUST be possible from messages, conversations, calls, contacts/accounts and relevant media where evidence is available.
Because native Connect messaging is E2EE, routine server-side moderation MUST NOT silently scan all decrypted private conversations. A participant-initiated report MAY deliberately disclose selected reported messages/media and the minimum necessary surrounding context/provenance to the Trust & Safety system. The reporting UI MUST make the disclosure scope understandable.
Reports are allegations, not strikes. A Report MUST NOT automatically become a verified violation or count as an offence merely because it exists. Trust & Safety must distinguish Report, Incident and EnforcementAction as separate canonical objects.
Reported user-supplied text, quoted messages, media metadata and report descriptions are evidence/input, not privileged instructions to the moderation system. Prompt-like content inside evidence MUST NOT be able to override moderation policy or system instructions.
Moderation AI
Connect MAY use an intelligent AI-assisted Trust & Safety evaluator to triage reports, correlate evidence, identify repeat patterns, create/maintain structured Incident records and recommend or apply policy-defined protective restrictions.
The moderation AI MUST NOT expose a direct free-form conversational prompt surface to ordinary users. Users interact through structured report/appeal flows; they MUST NOT be able to directly prompt the moderation model to punish another user.
The evaluator SHOULD produce structured results including alleged policy category, evidence reviewed, provenance, confidence/uncertainty, severity, verified prior Incidents where policy permits, pattern/repetition state, recommended action, automatic-action eligibility and human-review requirement. User accusation volume alone MUST NOT be treated as proof.
Automatic detection/evaluation MUST resist coordinated false-report campaigns, duplicate-report amplification, fabricated evidence where provenance can be checked, prompt injection within evidence and circular reliance on previous unverified allegations. Dismissed/overturned reports/incidents MUST NOT continue increasing enforcement severity.
Protective restrictions MAY be applied quickly when needed to stop ongoing harm, including reporter-specific contact blocking, temporary DM/call restrictions, new-contact limits, invitation restrictions, media restrictions or rate limits. These temporary protections are distinct from a Connect-wide ban.
Severe-offence ban threshold
A Connect-wide account ban is a last-resort enforcement action reserved for severe offences or a substantial verified history of serious misconduct. Ordinary disagreements, unpopular opinions, isolated low-level rudeness or weak/ambiguous reports MUST NOT result in a Connect-wide ban.
Ban-eligible examples include accounts demonstrably operated primarily for scams/phishing or large-scale malicious spam; repeated targeted harassment/stalking/doxxing; repeated serious threats or malicious impersonation/scams; distribution of illegal images/content; or comparably severe abuse supported by evidence and applicable policy.
A substantial history means verified Incident records, not raw Report count. Multiple unverified or dismissed reports MUST NOT accumulate as though they were convictions.
Enforcement SHOULD be proportionate below the severe-ban threshold and MAY include warnings, temporary communication restrictions, feature-specific suspension, contact/request limits, group-invite restrictions, rate limiting or temporary account suspension according to policy.
Every ban MUST reference the applicable policy category, supporting IncidentIDs/evidence basis, decision source, effective time, duration/permanence, review status and appeal state. The system MUST preserve the distinction between evidence, analysis and final enforcement.
Permanent or long-duration account-wide sanctions SHOULD require stronger evidentiary confidence and/or human review according to severity and policy. Clearly malicious automated/scam accounts with strong evidence MAY be restricted rapidly without artificial delay merely because the final action is severe.
Appeals
Affected users MUST have a clear appeal mechanism for significant restrictions and bans. Appeal review MUST inspect the evidence and enforcement decision rather than merely rerun the identical model prompt and automatically return the same result.
Overturned enforcement MUST remove or appropriately quarantine the sanction's contribution to future escalation/ban-evasion logic. Audit history MAY retain the historical decision for accountability, but it MUST NOT continue operating as an active verified offence.
Ban-evasion and alternate-account detection
An active Connect ban MUST NOT be trivially circumventable by creating or switching to another account. Connect MUST provide a privacy-preserving Ban Evasion Risk Engine capable of identifying likely alternate accounts used to evade an active severe sanction.
Detection MUST be purpose-limited to security/abuse enforcement and MUST comply with the Privacy Ceiling. It SHOULD combine multiple relevant signals rather than relying on one simplistic identifier. Signals MAY include verified account relationships, device/account linkage legitimately available to 9to1, authentication attributes, repeated malicious behavioural patterns, overlap of abuse targets, timing patterns, organisation relationships and payment/entitlement linkage where applicable.
Shared IP address, household, school/workplace network, carrier NAT, VPN use or a shared device MUST NOT by itself establish that two accounts belong to the same banned person. Legitimate possession of multiple accounts is not ban evasion.
The engine MUST distinguish low-, medium- and high-confidence linkage. Low-confidence matches SHOULD trigger additional verification, monitoring within permitted bounds or temporary protective limits rather than automatic permanent inheritance of the original ban. High-confidence evidence tied to a severe active ban MAY cause the alternate account to inherit/continue the restriction according to policy.
Every suspected linkage MUST create a BanEvasionCase with evidence/signal references, original EnforcementActionID, confidence, decision and review/appeal state. Banned-account linkage MUST NOT depend on weakening E2EE or reading unrelated private messages.
Signals from an overturned/dismissed ban MUST be removed from active enforcement decisions. Anti-alt detection MUST NOT evolve into a general-purpose cross-service fingerprinting system unrelated to preventing sanction evasion.
AI and encrypted communication boundary
Dulche MAY assist with permitted Connect tasks such as drafting, summarisation, search, action extraction and organisation, but encrypted communication content is not automatically AI context. The user/organisation policy and the local/cloud Privacy Ceiling determine what content may be exposed.
A local AI route MAY process authorised content locally according to permissions. Sending decrypted chat/call/email content to a cloud model requires an authorised cloud-processing route and MUST NOT occur merely because the cloud model is the global fallback.
AI-generated actions that send messages, email, make calls, change membership, report users or perform enforcement are consequential typed actions subject to the normal Home permission/risk model plus any stricter Connect rule.
Agent updates — contact through Connect
Agents MUST be emailable, callable and textable through Connect. This includes email through Connect's Mail subsystem, supported voice-call routes, and text messaging through Connect, including SMS/RCS when an authorised configured provider/device supports that transport. Agents MUST appear as addressable Agent contacts rather than requiring users to open a separate Agent chat before contacting them.
Channel addresses/endpoints MUST resolve to the same canonical Agent identity. Incoming contact MUST route to that Agent and its authorised runtime; responses MUST return through the relevant Connect channel with conversation/call/run correlation. Agent permissions, memory boundaries, caller access, availability, privacy, retention and external-action approvals remain governed by the existing contracts. A message or call from a third party MUST NOT automatically acquire the account owner's permissions. Unsupported or disconnected transports MUST be reported accurately. Provisioning paid numbers, carrier services or other paid infrastructure requires separate spending authorisation.
Connect Agent-channel API and acceptance
Extend Connect’s existing contact and communication APIs for Agent contact/channel configuration, endpoint resolution and the supported email, voice-call and text operations. Preserve canonical Agent, Conversation, Call and Run IDs, permission scopes, correlation and idempotency on retries. Tests MUST deliver an email, call and text to the intended canonical Agent through each supported configured route and verify its response on that route; cover revoked caller access, disconnected or unsupported transport, failed delivery and prevention of duplicate external sends. A required route lacking a working supported implementation remains an explicit gap, not a completed parity claim.

SMS and RCS
Connect MUST support SMS and RCS where the current platform, telephony stack, carrier/provider and user permissions allow it. SMS/RCS identities and transport state MUST remain distinct from native Connect messaging.
The UI MUST truthfully represent the protection of the actual transport used. Ordinary SMS MUST NOT be labelled end-to-end encrypted. RCS MUST show E2EE only when encryption has actually been negotiated/supported for that conversation and participant set.
If an intended RCS message would fall back to SMS, any material change in privacy/security capability MUST be represented clearly enough that the user is not led to believe the stronger state still applies. Transport fallback MUST NOT reuse an E2EE badge/state from the prior route.
Voice and video calling
Connect MUST provide mature one-to-one and group voice/video calling with expected modern functionality including incoming/outgoing calls, ringing, missed calls, call history, join/leave/reconnect, participant roster, grid/speaker layouts, pin/spotlight where applicable, microphone mute/unmute, camera enable/disable, camera switching, input/output device selection, screen/window/application sharing, optional system-audio sharing where supported, reactions, raise hand, in-call text chat, picture-in-picture/full-screen and accessible keyboard/screen-reader controls.
Calls MUST use end-to-end encrypted media wherever the selected call architecture supports the native Connect trust model. Signalling and sensitive call state SHOULD receive equivalent or stronger protection where technically feasible. Infrastructure MUST NOT claim stronger privacy than the actual transport provides.
Microphone, camera and screen-capture permissions MUST be explicit, visible and revocable. Joining a call MUST NOT silently enable the camera or microphone contrary to the user's saved/default state. The UI MUST continuously and unmistakably show local mic/camera/screen-share state.
Call infrastructure MUST minimise retained metadata, and self-hosted/private infrastructure SHOULD be supported where compatible with the donor/protocol architecture. TURN/relay/direct-connect behaviour and the associated exposure of participant network addresses MUST be documented and privacy-aware.
Background blur, noise suppression, gain control, camera filters/effects, virtual backgrounds and similar media processing SHOULD run locally where technically practical. A cosmetic filter MUST NOT silently upload raw camera/microphone content to an external processor.
Recording, transcription and AI participation
Recording is disabled by default. Starting recording MUST use a Request Recording workflow rather than an immediate unilateral record action.
Before recording begins, every current participant MUST explicitly approve the recording request. Any participant declining or failing to approve within the defined request state prevents recording from starting. Approval is scoped to that recording session and MUST NOT become a permanent blanket permission.
When recording is active, all participants MUST receive a persistent, unmistakable recording indicator. A participant joining after recording has started MUST be informed before/while joining that recording is active and MUST explicitly acknowledge/approve participation under the recording state before their media is included. A new participant's refusal MUST prevent their media from being recorded and, where the architecture cannot isolate them, MUST pause/stop recording until consent is resolved.
Recording state, requester, participant approvals, start/stop times and resulting artifact identity MUST be auditable. Recordings MUST be stored as permissioned canonical artifacts with explicit owner/access/retention policy rather than hidden provider blobs.
Recording permission MUST NOT imply permission for transcription, AI summarisation or remote model processing. Recording, transcription and AI participation are separate capabilities with separate disclosure/permission requirements.
Adding Dulche, an Agent, transcription service or other non-human processor to a human conversation/call MUST be visible to affected participants where it can receive their communication. Ordinary access by the local Connect client to decrypted E2EE content does NOT automatically grant Dulche/cloud models access.
Contact and communication privacy controls
Connect MUST provide first-class Block, Mute and Contact Settings controls. Blocking and muting MUST be semantically distinct: mute suppresses attention/notifications according to user policy; block prevents the blocked identity from contacting/interacting with the blocker through applicable Connect channels and MUST be enforced beyond merely hiding content locally.
Contact Settings MUST allow the user to control, where applicable, who can directly message them, call them, video call them, add/invite them to groups, see presence/last-active, see read receipts and access profile/contact fields. Unknown contacts MAY be routed to message/contact requests rather than the primary inbox.
Per-conversation notification/mute controls, read-receipt controls, presence controls, privacy/discoverability controls and block lists MUST be available without requiring AI.
Reporting and Trust & Safety
Connect MUST provide a first-class Report workflow for inappropriate, abusive, fraudulent or illegal content/behaviour. Reporting MUST be possible from messages, conversations, calls, contacts/accounts and relevant media where evidence is available.
Because native Connect messaging is E2EE, routine server-side moderation MUST NOT silently scan all decrypted private conversations. A participant-initiated report MAY deliberately disclose selected reported messages/media and the minimum necessary surrounding context/provenance to the Trust & Safety system. The reporting UI MUST make the disclosure scope understandable.
Reports are allegations, not strikes. A Report MUST NOT automatically become a verified violation or count as an offence merely because it exists. Trust & Safety must distinguish Report, Incident and EnforcementAction as separate canonical objects.
Reported user-supplied text, quoted messages, media metadata and report descriptions are evidence/input, not privileged instructions to the moderation system. Prompt-like content inside evidence MUST NOT be able to override moderation policy or system instructions.
Moderation AI
Connect MAY use an intelligent AI-assisted Trust & Safety evaluator to triage reports, correlate evidence, identify repeat patterns, create/maintain structured Incident records and recommend or apply policy-defined protective restrictions.
The moderation AI MUST NOT expose a direct free-form conversational prompt surface to ordinary users. Users interact through structured report/appeal flows; they MUST NOT be able to directly prompt the moderation model to punish another user.
The evaluator SHOULD produce structured results including alleged policy category, evidence reviewed, provenance, confidence/uncertainty, severity, verified prior Incidents where policy permits, pattern/repetition state, recommended action, automatic-action eligibility and human-review requirement. User accusation volume alone MUST NOT be treated as proof.
Automatic detection/evaluation MUST resist coordinated false-report campaigns, duplicate-report amplification, fabricated evidence where provenance can be checked, prompt injection within evidence and circular reliance on previous unverified allegations. Dismissed/overturned reports/incidents MUST NOT continue increasing enforcement severity.
Protective restrictions MAY be applied quickly when needed to stop ongoing harm, including reporter-specific contact blocking, temporary DM/call restrictions, new-contact limits, invitation restrictions, media restrictions or rate limits. These temporary protections are distinct from a Connect-wide ban.
Severe-offence ban threshold
A Connect-wide account ban is a last-resort enforcement action reserved for severe offences or a substantial verified history of serious misconduct. Ordinary disagreements, unpopular opinions, isolated low-level rudeness or weak/ambiguous reports MUST NOT result in a Connect-wide ban.
Ban-eligible examples include accounts demonstrably operated primarily for scams/phishing or large-scale malicious spam; repeated targeted harassment/stalking/doxxing; repeated serious threats or malicious impersonation/scams; distribution of illegal images/content; or comparably severe abuse supported by evidence and applicable policy.
A substantial history means verified Incident records, not raw Report count. Multiple unverified or dismissed reports MUST NOT accumulate as though they were convictions.
Enforcement SHOULD be proportionate below the severe-ban threshold and MAY include warnings, temporary communication restrictions, feature-specific suspension, contact/request limits, group-invite restrictions, rate limiting or temporary account suspension according to policy.
Every ban MUST reference the applicable policy category, supporting IncidentIDs/evidence basis, decision source, effective time, duration/permanence, review status and appeal state. The system MUST preserve the distinction between evidence, analysis and final enforcement.
Permanent or long-duration account-wide sanctions SHOULD require stronger evidentiary confidence and/or human review according to severity and policy. Clearly malicious automated/scam accounts with strong evidence MAY be restricted rapidly without artificial delay merely because the final action is severe.
Appeals
Affected users MUST have a clear appeal mechanism for significant restrictions and bans. Appeal review MUST inspect the evidence and enforcement decision rather than merely rerun the identical model prompt and automatically return the same result.
Overturned enforcement MUST remove or appropriately quarantine the sanction's contribution to future escalation/ban-evasion logic. Audit history MAY retain the historical decision for accountability, but it MUST NOT continue operating as an active verified offence.
Ban-evasion and alternate-account detection
An active Connect ban MUST NOT be trivially circumventable by creating or switching to another account. Connect MUST provide a privacy-preserving Ban Evasion Risk Engine capable of identifying likely alternate accounts used to evade an active severe sanction.
Detection MUST be purpose-limited to security/abuse enforcement and MUST comply with the Privacy Ceiling. It SHOULD combine multiple relevant signals rather than relying on one simplistic identifier. Signals MAY include verified account relationships, device/account linkage legitimately available to 9to1, authentication attributes, repeated malicious behavioural patterns, overlap of abuse targets, timing patterns, organisation relationships and payment/entitlement linkage where applicable.
Shared IP address, household, school/workplace network, carrier NAT, VPN use or a shared device MUST NOT by itself establish that two accounts belong to the same banned person. Legitimate possession of multiple accounts is not ban evasion.
The engine MUST distinguish low-, medium- and high-confidence linkage. Low-confidence matches SHOULD trigger additional verification, monitoring within permitted bounds or temporary protective limits rather than automatic permanent inheritance of the original ban. High-confidence evidence tied to a severe active ban MAY cause the alternate account to inherit/continue the restriction according to policy.
Every suspected linkage MUST create a BanEvasionCase with evidence/signal references, original EnforcementActionID, confidence, decision and review/appeal state. Banned-account linkage MUST NOT depend on weakening E2EE or reading unrelated private messages.
Signals from an overturned/dismissed ban MUST be removed from active enforcement decisions. Anti-alt detection MUST NOT evolve into a general-purpose cross-service fingerprinting system unrelated to preventing sanction evasion.
AI and encrypted communication boundary
Dulche MAY assist with permitted Connect tasks such as drafting, summarisation, search, action extraction and organisation, but encrypted communication content is not automatically AI context. The user/organisation policy and the local/cloud Privacy Ceiling determine what content may be exposed.
A local AI route MAY process authorised content locally according to permissions. Sending decrypted chat/call/email content to a cloud model requires an authorised cloud-processing route and MUST NOT occur merely because the cloud model is the global fallback.
AI-generated actions that send messages, email, make calls, change membership, report users or perform enforcement are consequential typed actions subject to the normal Home permission/risk model plus any stricter Connect rule.
Agent updates — contact through Connect
Agents MUST be emailable, callable and textable through Connect. This includes email through Connect's Mail subsystem, supported voice-call routes, and text messaging through Connect, including SMS/RCS when an authorised configured provider/device supports that transport. Agents MUST appear as addressable Agent contacts rather than requiring users to open a separate Agent chat before contacting them.
Channel addresses/endpoints MUST resolve to the same canonical Agent identity. Incoming contact MUST route to that Agent and its authorised runtime; responses MUST return through the relevant Connect channel with conversation/call/run correlation. Agent permissions, memory boundaries, caller access, availability, privacy, retention and external-action approvals remain governed by the existing contracts. A message or call from a third party MUST NOT automatically acquire the account owner's permissions. Unsupported or disconnected transports MUST be reported accurately. Provisioning paid numbers, carrier services or other paid infrastructure requires separate spending authorisation.
Connect Agent-channel API and acceptance
Extend Connect’s existing contact and communication APIs for Agent contact/channel configuration, endpoint resolution and the supported email, voice-call and text operations. Preserve canonical Agent, Conversation, Call and Run IDs, permission scopes, correlation and idempotency on retries. Tests MUST deliver an email, call and text to the intended canonical Agent through each supported configured route and verify its response on that route; cover revoked caller access, disconnected or unsupported transport, failed delivery and prevention of duplicate external sends. A required route lacking a working supported implementation remains an explicit gap, not a completed parity claim.

original_text:
Mail is implementation-complete only when acceptance coverage verifies at least:
* The final UI passes dedicated visual QA for a cohesive modern 9to1 CUI shell with responsive pane behaviour, clean message/compose surfaces, consistent spacing/typography and no exposed legacy donor UI.
* Applicable mature donor email capabilities are accounted for in the donor-parity manifest independently from visual design.
* At least Gmail/Google, Outlook/Microsoft and generic IMAP+SMTP accounts can coexist with Unified Inbox without provider-semantics loss.
* Gmail-style label semantics and generic IMAP folder semantics remain distinguishable and correct.
* Incremental push/IDLE/provider sync updates a connected mailbox without complete rescans for ordinary changes.
* Offline cached mail is readable and queued mutations survive app/device restart then reconcile on reconnect.
* Draft autosave/recovery preserves content and surfaces provider/local conflicts rather than overwriting silently.
* Offline send enters Outbox/Queued and send failure remains visible/retryable rather than being reported Sent.
* Client-side Undo Send cancels before provider submission and stops presenting undo once sending is irreversible.
* Scheduled send accurately identifies provider/cloud/device execution semantics and does not imply guarantees the selected executor cannot provide.
* Attachments can be opened/saved through Files and Attach from Files works with authorised local/9to1 Drive content.
* Search works across the defined fields and saved smart views do not duplicate messages.
* Remote email HTML/script cannot execute trusted app code and remote-image tracking obeys privacy controls.
* OpenPGP/S/MIME donor-supported behaviour works or has an explicit scoped parity exception.
* The AI bar can summarise/draft against explicit context while respecting local/cloud privacy policy.
* AI cannot bypass Mail.Send permission simply because it drafted a message.
* Provider reauthentication/revocation does not erase valid cached messages/drafts.
* Home notification deep links open the exact intended message/thread/account.
* Home/Dulche service restart produces a recoverable/degraded state without mailbox database corruption.
* Core UI operations and provider actions have equivalent typed API coverage.
