LE-10 — Cards canonical product contract
Cards is a first-party CUI app. No external app donor is selected by this section. It MUST ship through the normal app catalogue, modular installer, Files/open-with and registered preview/editor paths, with the global launch screen, settings, permissions and contextual AI bar. Windows, 9to1-OS and web retain the same canonical flashcard model; other already-supported client obligations remain active. A platform constraint must be declared and tested, not hidden behind an empty app shell or assumed mobile fallback.
A CardSet has stable SetID/ArtifactID, title, owner/scope, ordered CardID membership, subject/topic references, assets and schema/revision metadata. Each Card has stable CardID, editable Front and Back structured content, metadata and revision. Sets and topics organise the same cards; changing a view/grouping does not duplicate content. Shared deck content and a user's ReviewRecord are distinct: review state records principal, CardID, optional TopicID, red/amber/green rating, evidence type and reviewed-at time without publishing another learner's private progress.
Front/back content MUST preserve the specified formatting, font choice, background colour, images, graphs and freehand ink as editable structured data through the Shared Productivity Engine and owning object contracts. Markdown-like formatting is a visual authoring capability, not permission to flatten graphs/ink into text. Native save/export is versioned and round-trips all supported data. Import/export reports unsupported constructs and preserves the source; it does not silently discard unknown required fields.
Required operations are create/open/save, edit either side, add/duplicate/reorder/remove/restore cards, bulk create/edit, search/filter, set/topic/custom grouping, asset insertion, drawing, rate/review, import/export and settings. Bulk edits expose exact per-item results where partial success is allowed; destructive bulk changes have impact preview and the inherited approval rules. Undo/redo and interrupted-save recovery preserve the prior valid revision.
The focused-card view retains partially visible, shadowed neighbours. Vertical scrolling is the default; horizontal navigation is a persisted option. Provide keyboard/touch navigation, the floating search bar and the subject/topic sidebar without obstructing content. Edit mode uses click-to-edit and an explicit Flip button. View mode uses click-to-flip and cannot mutate card content; rating is permitted as personal review state. The AI bar's Write setting does not override the host's View restriction.
A rating MUST persist on the card's personal review record. When a valid Study topic link exists, it MUST submit attributed evidence to the existing Study service and update linked views. An unlinked card remains usable and offers topic linking rather than fabricating a mapping. Shared deck edits do not overwrite other users' review records. Inline Spaces flashcards and Revision Bank entries must be able to open/save the same canonical set.
Acceptance: create a multi-card set with distinct front/back text, rich formatting, image, graph and ink; bulk edit and undo; switch navigation/grouping; search; save/restart and native export/import without loss; prove View cannot edit; rate linked and unlinked cards; verify Study linkage, private per-user reviews, shared-edit conflicts, crash recovery and the same set in Cards, Spaces and Revision Bank. Large sets MUST virtualise card views and bound image/graph/ink caches.

original_text:
LE-11 — Planner Burrows contract
A Burrow is a named planning context over existing Planner entities, not a duplicate calendar engine or a copy of events/tasks/assignments. It has stable BurrowID, name/icon, owner/scope, ordering, archive state and revision. Native items may have one BurrowID or be Unassigned; the All view includes authorised items across burrows without duplicate identities. Existing items remain Unassigned unless the user assigns them or an existing explicit association provides a deterministic migration.
Study has one canonical Study burrow per owning Study scope, created idempotently and referenced by ID rather than the display name. A custom Minecraft burrow is an independent user-created context. Study's Planner button opens its Study burrow inside the real Planner surface, and Open in App preserves the burrow selection and canonical item identities.
Users MUST be able to create, rename, reorder, select, set a default, archive/recover and delete a burrow; assign/reassign/unassign existing events, PlannerTasks, assignments and other supported planning items; and filter normal Planner views by burrow or All/Unassigned. New items created within a selected burrow inherit that assignment. Moving between burrows changes organisation only, not event time, recurrence, provider calendar, attendees or reminder identity.
Provider-backed items retain provider IDs and permissions. Burrow membership may be local 9to1 metadata and MUST NOT silently move or duplicate the external item. Recurring-item assignment requires an explicit occurrence/series scope using Planner's existing recurrence rules. A burrow's visibility never grants access to otherwise private contained items.
Deleting a burrow MUST preview its item count and reassign its items to a chosen authorised burrow or Unassigned; it must not delete the events/tasks/assignments. Archive hides the context without destroying membership. Reminders continue under existing item policies, regardless of whether a burrow is currently visible.
Acceptance: keep Study and Minecraft items distinct while All shows both once; create and move items without changed IDs/times/reminders; restart; edit a recurring series with explicit scope; handle a read-only external event's local grouping; delete/recover a burrow without losing planning items; verify embedded and standalone Planner use the same state.

original_text:
LE-12 — API, state and failure contracts
Every new UI action MUST use the same typed domain operation as automation. Extend existing namespaces rather than introducing parallel services: Home package install/update/repair; Spaces Sidebar sections/items/rules, Tabs, conversation placement/transfers, Study recommendations and RevisionBank; 9to1.Cards sets/cards/content/reviews; and 9to1.Planner.Burrows with Create, Get, List, Update, Assign, Unassign, Archive, Restore and Delete.
Before consumers implement against them, owners MUST publish the versioned action catalogue with exact argument/result schemas, affected stable IDs, owner/scope, required permissions, risk/reversibility, expectedRevision for writes, pagination for lists and operationId for replayable mutations. Long operations return JobID/status/cancellation and per-target outcomes. Read/search/preview/context and write APIs enforce the same current permissions; client-supplied account, Space or Burrow IDs do not grant access.
At minimum expose the UI-equivalent create/read/update/organise/delete/recover/import/export/configuration actions, Cards Rate and review queries, RevisionBank Add/Remove/Classify/Recommend/Create/Open, Sidebar AddSection/AddItem/Move/SetRule/Reset, Tabs Open/Select/Move/Close/Restore, and conversation GetPlacement/SetPlacement/SendToCloud/SendToDevice/GetTransfer/CancelTransfer. Public naming must remain within the existing canonical namespace conventions. Internal representations may vary only if these observable semantics remain compatible.
Use the existing structured error envelope. Add specific codes where absent for DependencyRequired, PackageDependencyConflict, TabTargetUnavailable, SidebarRuleInvalid, ProtectedSidebarItem, StorageModeDenied, TemporaryChatMustBeSaved, EntitlementRequired, QuotaExceeded, DeviceRevoked, TransferInterrupted, RevisionConflict, ResourceUnavailable, UnsupportedCardContent and BurrowNotFound. Errors identify action/target, retryability, retained source state and any completed/failed/skipped targets. Unknown/unavailable values are not fabricated defaults.
Persistent schemas MUST be versioned, revision-aware and crash-safe. Permission checks occur again on reconnect/commit. Repeated requests do not duplicate sets, memberships, planning items or transfers. Independent edits can merge only under the owning contract; conflicting edits preserve recoverable versions or return an explicit conflict. Normal deletion is recoverable; permanent purge remains a separate elevated operation. Migrations inspect and preserve actual existing data rather than assuming there is none.
LE-13 — Worker ownership and integration order
The coordinator first maps inherited requirements and affected source areas, then agrees shared manifests/APIs and test fixtures. Assign bounded owners for package/runtime modularity; Spaces navigation/sidebar/tabs/usage; conversation placement/privacy; Study/Revision Bank/Cards; and Planner Burrows. Workers may proceed in parallel only with non-overlapping owned files or explicit coordination. Consumers use reviewed interfaces, not independently invented schemas or duplicate shared components.
Integrate completed units continuously into the accepted root with owning tests and exact-head regression checks. Validate a shared component before dependent surfaces claim completion. 2026-10-09 — APPROVED ASSISTANTS, SPECIALISTS, CONNECT AND INLINE COMMAND REQUIREMENTS
Assistants are persistent configurable conversational identities, distinct from job-defined reusable Specialists. Each Assistant owns multiple persistent conversation threads, with create, rename, switch, search, pin, archive, delete and branch management. Thread history and work context are separate, while Assistant-level memory and permitted cross-thread retrieval are shared. Spaces and Assistants open the same canonical threads and Task/Runs without copying state.
All 9to1 chat services must automatically compact working context while retaining complete original messages and retrievable history, so conversations can continue for months or years without arbitrary message-count caps. Finite model context and resource limitations must be handled honestly; summaries must never replace source history.
Assistants must retain all inherited Agents functionality, with complete feature-parity auditing and user-facing management for identity, instructions, knowledge/files, memory, models, tools/apps, Skills, Quick Actions, permissions, approvals, budgets, queues, delegation, history, background execution, steering, recovery, proactive contact and optional Mini Computer. Support configuration revision history, data lifecycle controls, search, durable artifacts, notifications and concurrent tasks.
Connect is the 9to1 communications app (email, chat and supported calls), not the external integration manager. Assistants and Specialists are selectable addressable contacts. Users can type an Assistant name into an email recipient field or message/call them. Responses stay in the originating channel and thread: email replies to email, chat to chat, calls in calls. The same Assistant identity and authorised work remain accessible in the Assistants app; approvals and notifications may surface separately without moving the primary reply.
Across supported 9to1 composers, @ opens a searchable picker for Assistants, Specialists and supported apps (such as Write and Present). A bare mention is passive and does not execute. An explicitly bounded instruction, for example @Present [Create five slides from this report], is a structured compact INLINE rich-text command, not a separate block editor, card or paragraph. Only that mention and its instruction are specially formatted; surrounding text remains normal, and typing resumes normally after the command. Support multiple commands in one paragraph, wrapping, editing, keyboard accessibility, persistence, copying and canonical identity. Preserve exact boundaries so ordinary text cannot accidentally execute. Commands respect Home permissions, approvals and revocation.
Implement and accept these as complete vertical product features with usable UI, backing behaviour, persistence, integration and real tests, not just architecture or compilation. Preserve existing compliant infrastructure and all earlier specification requirements.

RCVP includes all non-exempt donor functionality and everything necessary for genuine everyday use: canonical CUI, launch/create/open/edit/save/close/reopen/export as applicable, accessible navigation, permissions, security, persistence, recovery, error handling, essential integrations and supported formats. Full adds 9to1-specific differentiating enhancements such as generative UI, unless a specific enhancement is explicitly essential to baseline functionality. Every feature is assigned to RCVP or Full in an approved per-app manifest; unassigned necessary features cannot silently be deferred. The four-part delivery order remains unchanged.

original_text: ACCEPT-001 — Real-feature proof. A feature is VERIFIED only when a real user can perform its complete intended workflow in the actual packaged application using genuine engines/providers and persistent state where applicable, with correct results, error handling and reopen/recovery checks. Unit tests, source presence, mock responses, screenshots or disconnected harnesses alone are insufficient. Where a live provider cannot be exercised, report NOT VERIFIED or BLOCKED, never simulate a PASS. Independent acceptance uses the specification and feature inventory, not only implementer-authored tests. Record artifact/build hash, platform, test steps, observed outcomes, screenshots where relevant, defects and reviewer.

original_text: ACCEPT-003 — Security and Dulche privacy. Cross-app personal context is denied by default and shared only following granular, informed, revocable user permission. Encrypt sensitive stored context and protected transfers; minimise data exposed to models and providers. Applications and non-model APIs must not receive protected Den context without explicit permission. Enforce these boundaries technically at runtime; model instructions alone are not a security boundary. Test denied, allowed, revoked, offline and provider-failure cases. Never claim a model can guarantee secrecy solely by being instructed not to relay data.

original_text: GOV-001 — Precedence and ambiguity handling. Later explicit owner-approved normative directives override earlier conflicting instructions only in their stated scope; historical schedules do not supersede the active four-part plan. Preserve all compatible prior requirements. If two requirements conflict, an implementation detail is unspecified, a donor feature cannot be reproduced or a quality threshold is absent, log the precise ambiguity and options, stop the affected acceptance decision and obtain owner approval. original_text: CUI-PRO-201 — Avalonia and Skia are retained as backend technology for rendering, input, layout, text shaping, windowing, composition and accessibility. They are NOT allowed to supply a visible FluentTheme, SimpleTheme, default Avalonia/AXAML template, selector/resource precedence, inherited popup chrome or donor styling for first-party CUI surfaces. All active native and browser CUI-hosted applications, including Present, MUST use CUI-owned typed templates, materials, semantic tokens, states and lifecycle. Audit the actual application startup, resource dictionaries, templated subclasses, menus, popups, tooltips, sliders, scrollbars, numeric inputs, accessibility and specialised canvases. Reject missing CUI templates rather than falling back to native. Legacy native Present entrypoints still using Fluent must be migrated to compliant CUI appearance without losing existing behaviour, or explicitly quarantined as incomplete; deleting Fluent imports while breaking control behaviour is not a fix.

original_text: CUI-PRO-202 — Professional reference. The owner's target image specifies a calm, neutral charcoal/superdark editor, darker inset stage, subtly brighter and softly elevated floating tools, white document title, muted grey secondary text, Montserrat throughout ordinary UI, disciplined whitespace, clear logical grouping, restrained outlines, slightly rounded inputs and generously rounded menus/floating surfaces. Shared icons should be coherent vector assets with consistent weight, precise alignment and honest hit areas. Hover, focus, pressed, selected, disabled and validation states must be visible, consistent and accessible. Avoid Windows-Fluent blue/grey tint, native-style widgets, mismatched fonts, uneven padding, accidental wrapping or controls made to look professional only through application-local colour patches. These principles belong in shared Professional tokens/templates, not separate hard-coded per-app workarounds.

SPUI-133 — MODEL REASONING EFFORT DISPLAY
The percentage attached to the model name in the Spaces Chat compact picker (for example “Qwen 3.6 • 100%”) is the currently selected REASONING EFFORT LEVEL for that model/route, NOT quota, remaining usage, context-window fill, confidence, CPU/GPU utilisation or provider health.
The selected effective model's REAL provider/Dulche capability metadata determines the number N of discrete supported effort levels and whether reasoning is enabled/disabled or configurable. Show N distinct user-facing percentage choices, each mapped one-to-one, in increasing order, onto the N actual advertised effort levels:
  N=3: 35%, 70%, 100%.
  N=4: 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%.
  N=5: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100%.
For other N, present evenly distributed, legible percentages for each distinct advertised level without inventing unsupported options. The listed 3/4/5 mappings are canonical. Percentages are normalised UI LABELS for discrete provider-specific effort rankings, NOT a literal continuous strength measurement nor a supported percentage of model parameters or context tokens. Displayed options MUST remain bijective to advertised reasoning levels; selecting the first displayed preset MUST invoke the first actual level and not the second. Bind selection to the exact model/provider's stable level identity or ordinal, not to an arbitrary percentage passed through an incompatible floor(p*N/100) formula. When the user changes models, discover the new model's own reasoning/effort options and show only the eligible ones; validate inherited and explicit selections. If a model offers an independent reasoning enabled/disabled switch, honour and display its real on/off state. If no reasoning-effort control exists, do not fabricate a 100% control or suggest that reasoning is configurable. If a provider supplies effort tiers but no on/off switch, do not invent one. Setting changes must affect the actual subsequent Dulche requests and survive the appropriate request/conversation override lifecycle. Fail clearly for unsupported effort settings, never silently assume the backend accepted them.
IMPLEMENTATION NOTE: Existing V2 low-level SetReasoningLevel prose uses min(n−1, floor(p*n/100)) for arbitrary percentage inputs. That function would map the first displayed 35% (for three levels) to the SECOND tier and the first displayed 20% (for five tiers) to the SECOND tier. The canonical user-facing selector must therefore map directly to discrete provider effort LevelIDs/ordinals, not route preset labels through that old formula. Any arbitrary-percent legacy API compatibility must be separately specified/versioned rather than causing incorrect or duplicated preset selection.

SPUI-136 — SEPARATION OF CONTEXT AND REMOTE USAGE DISPLAY
The compact Spaces top-header progress-circle control remains immediately left of the Universal Model Picker when both are applicable. Its CONTEXT occupancy metric is separate from USAGE. Reasoning percentage beside model name (e.g. 100%) remains exclusively the currently selected model reasoning-effort tier and MUST NOT be re-used for quota or usage.
(a) LOCAL MODEL: The usage meter/arc MUST be HIDDEN. Context-window progress MAY remain visible when actual effective context capacity and consumption are known. The absence of a usage arc for local models must not imply absence of RAM/VRAM/runtime constraints; those have their own diagnostics. Do not display the M warning merely because a model is local.
(b) REMOTE/CLOUD MODEL WITH VERIFIED PROVIDER USAGE DATA: Show usage as a coloured progress arc only where a meaningful, trustworthy measured numerator and denominator are both available for the applicable scope/window. It can coexist with the differently coloured context metric. Tooltip/focus details identify scope (provider or model), resource/unit, window, value, limit, provider account, freshness/reset if applicable, and data provenance.
(c) REMOTE/CLOUD MODEL WITH NO PROVIDER USAGE DATA: HIDE the usage meter/arc and show an accessible compact “M” marker, indicating that the model is LIKELY METERED / may count towards an external allowance or billing but provider usage telemetry is unavailable. “M” is NOT itself evidence that billing is occurring. Hover/focus/tap explains “Provider usage unavailable; this model may still be metered”, plus any separately recorded 9to1-only custom budget state. M must not be displayed as a bogus zero percentage or a guessing ring. Keep independently measurable CONTEXT indicator visible, if available.
(d) Only one reliable metric in a circular indicator is allowed: display only that metric; do not render an empty second ring as though it is a measurable zero. If neither is measurable, show an informative unavailable state rather than fabricated measurements. Do not mix local usage with remote billing, and do not infer provider quotas from local tokens alone.
(e) Provider usage summaries, the separate LE-06 comprehensive sidebar usage UI and the Home Models usage limits are linked surfaces, not conflicting duplicate sources of truth. Hidden compact usage ring does NOT disable user-configured limit enforcement or local request accounting.

SPUI-136 — SEPARATION OF CONTEXT AND REMOTE USAGE DISPLAY
The compact Spaces top-header progress-circle control remains immediately left of the Universal Model Picker when both are applicable. Its CONTEXT occupancy metric is separate from USAGE. Reasoning percentage beside model name (e.g. 100%) remains exclusively the currently selected model reasoning-effort tier and MUST NOT be re-used for quota or usage.
(a) LOCAL MODEL: The usage meter/arc MUST be HIDDEN. Context-window progress MAY remain visible when actual effective context capacity and consumption are known. The absence of a usage arc for local models must not imply absence of RAM/VRAM/runtime constraints; those have their own diagnostics. Do not display the M warning merely because a model is local.
(b) REMOTE/CLOUD MODEL WITH VERIFIED PROVIDER USAGE DATA: Show usage as a coloured progress arc only where a meaningful, trustworthy measured numerator and denominator are both available for the applicable scope/window. It can coexist with the differently coloured context metric. Tooltip/focus details identify scope (provider or model), resource/unit, window, value, limit, provider account, freshness/reset if applicable, and data provenance.
(c) REMOTE/CLOUD MODEL WITH NO PROVIDER USAGE DATA: HIDE the usage meter/arc and show an accessible compact “M” marker, indicating that the model is LIKELY METERED / may count towards an external allowance or billing but provider usage telemetry is unavailable. “M” is NOT itself evidence that billing is occurring. Hover/focus/tap explains “Provider usage unavailable; this model may still be metered”, plus any separately recorded 9to1-only custom budget state. M must not be displayed as a bogus zero percentage or a guessing ring. Keep independently measurable CONTEXT indicator visible, if available.
(d) Only one reliable metric in a circular indicator is allowed: display only that metric; do not render an empty second ring as though it is a measurable zero. If neither is measurable, show an informative unavailable state rather than fabricated measurements. Do not mix local usage with remote billing, and do not infer provider quotas from local tokens alone.
(e) Provider usage summaries, the separate LE-06 comprehensive sidebar usage UI and the Home Models usage limits are linked surfaces, not conflicting duplicate sources of truth. Hidden compact usage ring does NOT disable user-configured limit enforcement or local request accounting.

SPUI-137 — LIMIT SCOPE: PROVIDER AND INDIVIDUAL MODEL
Home's canonical model/provider management MUST support USAGE LIMITS at BOTH independently selectable scopes:
  PROVIDER-SCOPED limit — applies to requests attributed to the specified configured provider/provider account and cumulatively covers all its applicable models/aliases/routes; identity is by stable ProviderID + Credential/Account Scope, never simply a display name. A separate provider account must not accidentally share or consume another account's budget.
  MODEL-SCOPED limit — applies only to the specific provider-scoped canonical ModelID (including aliases resolving to that identity), independent of other models from the same provider. Model-specific scope must remain unambiguous if multiple providers expose similar model names.
Both scopes can be active simultaneously. Each request updates relevant counters at most once and is checked against EVERY applicable limit; model and provider counts represent distinct aggregates, not additive charges. The effective allowed action is governed by all active applicable constraints. A model limit never overrides/weakens a provider limit, provider hard limit, account entitlement, organisational policy or external billing/provider quota. Provider budgets can be set/edited in Provider Settings; model budgets can be set/edited in that model's Home settings. A model editor may display inherited provider caps as read-only or navigable, clearly separated from model-specific caps.
Provider quotas reported by the provider and OWNER-DEFINED 9to1 custom limits are distinct provenance/source categories, not two representations of the same limit. Present source, scope and enforcement behaviour clearly.

Home → AI/Models → select model → Model Settings MUST expose a readable CUI-owned details/editor surface, including:

SPUI-139 — REPEATING USAGE LIMIT EDITOR
Both Model Settings and Provider Settings MUST provide a compact, editable, row-based usage-limit list with an explicit + Add Limit action.
Each Limit includes at least:
  Limit value: validated non-negative numeric bound appropriate to the metric.
  Metric/unit selector: Total Tokens, Input Tokens, Output Tokens, Tool Calls, Messages, Elapsed Time, and additional versioned extensible applicable resource metrics if supported.
  Period: “per” selected duration/window e.g. Day, Week, Month, or another supported configured interval.
  Scope/owner: Model-specific OR Provider/account-wide, visibly identified.
  Source: Provider-reported/Hard, User-defined Hard (locally enforced), or User-defined Advisory/Warning where supported.
  Active state, effective reset/timezone or rolling-window basis, observed/tracked usage, validity and error state.
Rows may be added, edited, disabled or removed with applicable confirmation and audit. Multiple limits of different units and periods coexist. They apply independently (e.g. 15 messages/week model cap AND 200,000 input tokens/month provider cap). Do NOT sum incommensurate units, roll distinct provider accounts together, or present a single magic combined remaining percentage. Limit scopes may be inherited by models from a provider, and both user-defined and provider-native limits must show which scopes apply. Tool-call definition, request/message counting and Elapsed Time semantics must have explicit stable accounting rules (e.g. actual elapsed wall-clock duration versus billable processing time) and honest provider capability support.

original_text:
SPUI-140 — COUNTING, ENFORCEMENT, FALLBACK, AND LIMIT TRANSPARENCY
User custom budgets MUST provide useful consumption control even when external providers do not expose quota telemetry. 9to1 may count its own authenticated request activity and measured token/tool/message/time metrics via Dulche, while labelling those values as “9to1-observed only” or Estimated when appropriate. It MUST NOT claim those numbers include all outside-provider usage or represent a real provider balance. In accordance with SPUI-136, lack of PROVIDER usage data still hides the compact remote usage arc and uses M, even when local tracked custom-budget usage can be inspected in Home or the indicator's detail surface.
When a custom limit is enforceable for 9to1-originated work, the router MUST check it before starting applicable requests and enforce it with authoritative shared counters for concurrency and retries, not merely grey out the UI. High-risk conflicting provider-side uncertainty must not be passed off as reliable hard cap. Advisory mode may warn without blocking; Hard mode blocks according to declared scope and period. Prior completed/pending actual usage must not be duplicated on retry, fallback or reconnection. When limits cannot be reliably counted/enforced, show “tracking unavailable” or require advisory mode; never promise a hard guarantee.
Provider usage signals can be delayed or partial; show observed-at/freshness and actual reason when a cap is unavailable/exhausted. Usage is attributed to the provider/model that ACTUALLY served the request after any authorised fallback, not simply the originally highlighted selection. Each applicable provider and model budget applies to whichever real backend processes the request, with no unauthorised local-to-cloud fallback.
Provider caps and user caps are independently enforced. Reaching one applicable cap blocks eligible traffic according to the relevant hard policy, even if another allowance still remains. A user-defined limit cannot increase a provider quota, paid entitlement or administrator restriction. Configurable warnings may trigger before thresholds, but their exact preset percentages are not fixed here.

The circular indicator's context progress uses effective context capacity for the actual selected/request-effective model, not the illustrative “Context: 670000 tokens” merely because that number is in a settings form. Unknown hidden provider overhead, context summarisation/retrieval and unobserved tokens require an estimated/unknown label. Usage colours are distinct from context colours in every CUI theme, with accessible text labels and focus/touch interaction. When multiple meaningful usage limits apply, any compact usage summary must clearly identify which ONE limit it depicts, while additional applicable limits are inspectable; never average tokens with elapsed time or combine providers without explanatory per-source details.
No part of this usage system changes the already owner-confirmed discrete reasoning-effort percentages of the Universal Model Picker.

SPUI-143 — DEFAULT LIMIT SELECTION (NO USER PIN)
The Spaces top-header USAGE progress circle presents the single MOST IMMEDIATELY CONSTRAINING applicable limit by the owner's two-stage decision rule, not the highest consumed percentage:
1. DEFAULT PREFERENCE: a SHORTER usage window takes precedence over a longer one (e.g. a five-hour limit is displayed before a weekly limit even if the five-hour cap is 20% used and the weekly cap is 80% used). Compare actual configured duration/windows, not the displayed percentage consumed.
2. SHORTER-WINDOW EXCEPTION: where an applicable longer-window cap has LESS ACTUAL REMAINING ALLOWANCE than the shorter-window cap IN COMPARABLE UNITS, the longer-window cap wins as it will constrain further equivalent use first. Example: weekly has 3,000 TOKENS left, five-hour cap has 5,000 TOKENS left; display weekly despite its longer window. The priority should account for imminent reset when its occurrence makes that cap non-blocking before the expected consumption.
3. Provider-wide and model-specific limits from both provider-reported and owner-defined settings MUST participate if they apply to the current effective model/provider account and have valid measurable data. Honor the source/telemetry visibility rules of SPUI-136: a local model hides usage; a remote model without provider-reported usage hides the compact usage arc and shows M rather than fabricating a fraction, even if a user custom cap can be separately inspected/enforced.
4. Never directly compare raw numeric remaining allowances of INCOMPATIBLE UNITS: tokens are not messages, time is not tool calls. A different-unit cap can outrank another only if a supported, transparent and sufficiently grounded forecast indicates the next effective blocking cap; otherwise use the time-window preference without pretending units are commensurable.
5. Actual blocking rules remain independent: all applicable enforceable caps are checked, regardless of which is displayed in the circle. Display choice must never switch off enforcement of hidden limits.

SPUI-144 — USER-PINNED LIMIT SELECTION
The user MUST be able to PIN exactly one applicable usage limit as the PREFERRED limit displayed in the usage circle. Pin controls belong in the usage breakdown/details popover and/or the corresponding Home model/provider usage settings. Visually distinguish selected pinned limit by a pin symbol and accessible label. Persist a stable canonical LimitID scoped to the relevant user/profile/provider account and model applicability (not the display name or an array index). Display the pinned limit by default regardless of another limit's percent filled, shorter reset window or routine dynamic selection.
PIN OVERRIDE — The pinned choice MUST be temporarily displaced ONLY when another enforceable applicable limit is credibly predicted or known to cause a meaningful, SOONER BLOCK of requests/use than the pinned limit. Example: user pinned five-hour tokens with 5,000 tokens remaining, but a weekly token limit has only 3,000 tokens remaining and is going to be exhausted first; display the weekly limit as an EMERGENT CONSTRAINT. A cap at 80% consumption does NOT override a pinned cap merely because its percentage exceeds the pinned cap's 20%. Account for reset windows and actual effective usage/forecast evidence, not percentages alone. If another limit cannot be confidently assessed, do not pretend there is an emergency.
Do NOT silently delete the stored pin just because an emergency temporarily takes the circle. Surface a clear “Temporarily showing weekly limit; five-hour limit remains pinned” notice, optionally with a warning/urgent symbol. Once the emergency has genuinely cleared (or the competing cap resets/is no longer the next blocker), restore the user's original pinned display automatically if eligible. If user explicitly unpins, the limit is permanently removed/unavailable, their scope changes or its permissions expire, fall back to default selection and explain why the saved preference is not currently active.
A pinned advisory/warning budget MAY be shown as a selected favourite but it MUST NOT supersede an actual imminent HARD cap capable of blocking requests. Multiple simultaneous candidates must be prioritised deterministically; no flickering/ring thrashing on every small telemetry update. Pin does not authorise external usage or change hard-quota enforcement.

SPUI-145 — TIME-TO-BLOCK EVIDENCE AND TOOLTIP
For comparable resource units, an actual lower remaining count can show which limit is encountered first under equivalent continued use. Where the system models projected exhaustion over time (especially across different units), it MUST use observable usage rate, active configured reset/window duration and request-specific measured or bounded costs where available, and label forecasts as estimated. Do not invent numerical thresholds, predict exact timing without sufficient data, or claim a remote provider allowance is known when it is not. The precise default urgency threshold/forecast confidence needed for “about to block” is STILL AN OPEN IMPLEMENTATION CHOICE; it must be explicitly decided before final hard-coded emergency-transition acceptance. Known imminent rejection of the current/next eligible request is sufficient to override a pin regardless of the exact warning horizon.
On hover/focus/tap, the usage indicator must reveal which active LIMIT is selected, the scope (provider-wide/model-specific), resource unit, window, actual remaining, current use/limit and reset if known, measurement source and freshness, PINNED status and, when temporarily overridden, the PINNED target plus reason the emergency blocker is currently displayed. Provide access to a full list of other applicable limits and their source/accuracy. Do not disguise usage/context ring identities or put the reasoning effort % in this tooltip as a usage gauge.

SPUI-147 — SHOWN TASKS SCOPE (OWNER CONFIRMED)
The Tasks Space contextual sidebar provides a discoverable 'Shown Tasks >' submenu through right-click/context menu and an equivalent accessible overflow/ellipsis menu. Its exactly specified scope choices are 'All Tasks' and 'Task Space Only'. DEFAULT for new users MUST be 'Task Space Only'. This reinforces that Spaces are first-party contextual work/conversation containers; using Tasks does not, by default, mean displaying every AI task from the whole account.
'Task Space Only' lists eligible canonical tasks originated within the Tasks Space. 'All Tasks' expands the view to other authorised canonical Tasks/Runs initiated through Chat and other Spaces/apps (for example Assistants, Specialists, Dev, Study or Automations where they create an actual TaskID). Choosing All Tasks is a DISPLAY/FILTER preference, not a migration, TaskID/RunID duplication, ownership conversion, extra background execution permission or a new task store. Opening a linked external task must resolve the SAME canonical TaskID, events, checkpoints, active workers, permissions and outputs, and preserve its originating context. Task visibility respects principal, workspace, account, project and storage scope; never reveal inaccessible tasks because 'All Tasks' is selected. The filter MUST NOT suspend hidden tasks or hide independently important user notifications/approval requests. Integrate the choice with existing revisioned Spaces sidebar/user-preference and CUI menus; expose both pointer context-click and keyboard/touch accessible equivalents. Do not confuse the sidebar scope filter with Chat type or Local/Mesh/Cloud storage location.

SPUI-149 — CANONICAL TASK TILE BADGES (OWNER CONFIRMED)
Each task tile displays a contextual PRIMARY task badge with the following owner-selected meanings, symbols and semantic colours (draw using CUI-owned icon/vector assets and current theme/accessibility tokens; emojis below are SYMBOLIC references, not a mandate to use multicolour emoji fonts):
• COMPLETED — tick/check, SHAMROCK green (✅); all agreed work has been produced but full acceptance verification is not yet satisfied.
• VERIFIED — tick/check, GOLD (✓); all agreed work has been produced and every applicable acceptance test passes for the current task/output revision. GOLD is the owner-confirmed distinct primary task-tile badge for VERIFIED; it is not interchangeable with shamrock COMPLETED. If a new requirement, changed output or stale/failed test invalidates verification, immediately withdraw the gold VERIFIED badge and show the truthful current status until reverified.
• UNREAD CHECKPOINT — flag, TURQUOISE (🏴 rendered turquoise). Show ONLY after a checkpoint is reached that the user has not yet viewed. Once the user views the newly reached checkpoint, remove the transient flag and show the task's current applicable progress/status indicator. Re-surface for a newly reached unread checkpoint. BLOCKED OVERRIDES the checkpoint flag.
• WORKING — animated person typing / at-work person (👨‍💻), truthful active substantial execution only. Honour reduced motion and non-animated accessibility fallback; never animate as 'working' when execution is disconnected/paused.
• PERMISSION NEEDED — BLUE shield (🛡️), linked to a real pending authorisation/permission gate; do not grant through appearance alone.
• STALLED — YELLOW warning triangle (⚠️), an unexpected problem the worker is actively trying to resolve without currently needing the user's intervention.
• BLOCKED — RED cross/no-entry (🚫), genuine material inability to proceed without the necessary external/person action. This badge takes precedence over an unread checkpoint flag.
Preserve underlying V2 distinction among raw Task states, execution stages, NEEDS INPUT, CHECKPOINT events, COMPLETED and VERIFIED acceptance status; the badge is a UI projection, not a replacement for the canonical schema. OWNER CONFIRMED 13 OCTOBER 2026: VERIFIED uses the distinct GOLD tick; COMPLETED retains the SHAMROCK-green tick. Continue showing accurate test/evidence status and the existing V2 gold verified checkpoint ticks. A completed-but-unverified Task must not display the VERIFIED gold tick. Other simultaneous-badge precedence beyond BLOCKED > unread CHECKPOINT is not yet owner-decided; maintain visible access to actionable pending approvals/questions regardless of the primary badge chosen.

SPUI-151 — QUICK QUESTIONS, APPROVALS AND PERMISSIONS (OWNER CONFIRMED)
An agent's question to the user adds a distinguishable inline task-tile action, visually a speech bubble containing a question mark (💬❔). Activating it opens a small Tasks-native CUI POP-OUT so the user can read the actual question, provide a short answer/choice, and return to the list without navigating to the entire Task Workspace. Responses must be securely associated with the correct TaskID/RunID/pending request, shown as RECEIVED versus APPLIED when not immediately consumed, delivered to the responsible agent at the next safe boundary, persisted/audited appropriately and reflected across widget/dashboard/chat views.
Likewise a real pending permission request must be actionable via the task tile/pop-out: the user can REVIEW the specific request and grant/deny only within the existing canonical Home/Dulche typed approval and permission boundaries. Surface requesting agent, intended action/target, scope, consequences and affected task, plus true approval state. Never implement a parallel permission broker or let a decorative one-click badge bypass required consent or authentication. A task may continue independent authorised work while awaiting one question or approval; the quick-action indicator and underlying execution status remain independently truthful. New actionable questions/permissions must remain discoverable even when a higher-priority primary status badge is visible.

SPUI-153 — TASKS SIDEBAR ACCEPTANCE / UNRESOLVED DESIGN REGISTER
MANDATORY REAL-RUNTIME CHECKS before claiming UI acceptance:
1. New user defaults to 'Task Space Only'; the Shown Tasks submenu toggles both scopes from right-click AND ellipsis/keyboard equivalents. Contextual sidebar customisations are not erased.
2. Start actual distinct Tasks from Tasks Space and from authorised external app/Chat origins. All Tasks shows permitted external tasks, Task Space Only excludes them, selecting any opens the SAME TaskID/RunIDs and preserves history/checkpoints/outputs; no duplicate Task or unauthorised visibility.
3. Verify realistic rich task tiles and ordering by genuine active state and priority under multiple simultaneous tasks, including pause, complete and blocked transitions. No hardcoded fake progress.
4. Exercise all seven owner-confirmed badge states: SHAMROCK-green COMPLETED tick, GOLD VERIFIED tick, TURQUOISE unread CHECKPOINT flag, animated WORKING person typing, BLUE PERMISSION NEEDED shield, YELLOW STALLED warning and RED BLOCKED cross. Verify real state transitions, no false gold VERIFIED after acceptance invalidation, reduced-motion fallback, and event-grounded hover/focus/tap details.
5. Reach a checkpoint without user viewing it: turquoise flag appears. Once actually viewed: return to current progress/status. Reach another: flag returns. If task becomes BLOCKED: red blocked badge displaces pending checkpoint flag without deleting the checkpoint event.
6. Inject a real pending agent question and answer through pop-out; demonstrate correct task binding, response/consumption state, recovery/navigation, and no destructive side effects.
7. Inject a real permission request, inspect/deny/grant through canonical provider-controlled approval UI; observe required auth/permission scope and whether unrelated work continues. Do not conflate NEEDS INPUT with BLOCKED.
8. Verify shamrock-green COMPLETED and gold VERIFIED task-tile ticks stay distinct; when actual evidence or the current acceptance set invalidates verification, the gold tick disappears until all applicable checks pass again.
9. Test long titles, multi-device/state updates, filtering during active work, hover/focus/touch, CUI theme inheritance (Professional/Glow), accessibility and small windows.
UNRESOLVED: precedence of simultaneous Permission Needed, Stalled, Working and unread Checkpoint outside confirmed Blocked-over-Checkpoint rule; precise definition of 'viewed' for checkpoint acknowledgement and how it syncs; tie-breaking/manual pin priority in sorting; exact visual arrangement/metadata of rich tiles. Do not invent final values.
END — TASKS SPACE SIDEBAR OWNER DECISIONS, 13 OCTOBER 2026.

SPUI-154 — PERMANENT MAIN CONVERSATION PER ASSISTANT (OWNER CONFIRMED)
Each persistent Assistant has exactly one auto-created primary conversation named “Main”. It is the Assistant's durable, personal, default conversation, conceptually like the ongoing conversation with a single contact in a messaging app. Selecting that Assistant normally opens Main rather than the last unrelated sub-conversation or an intermediary mandatory dashboard. Main retains its canonical ConversationID, Assistant identity, eligible history and authorised context across application navigation/restarts; creating or switching other chats must not silently recreate, replace, erase or split Main. The “Main” role/identity is permanent. Whether the visible label may be user-renamed while preserving the Main role is NOT YET DECIDED; do not imply a disposable Main.
The Assistant may have multiple ADDITIONAL conversations with their own titles, histories, current work/context and canonical ConversationIDs, used to organise projects and specialised topics. These belong to the same persistent Assistant identity and share only the Assistant-level memories, configured policies, permissions and cross-thread references actually authorised. Main is not an aggregate transcript of every sub-conversation. Preserve existing approved thread operations on eligible non-Main chats (create/rename/search/pin/archive/delete/branch etc) while protecting Main's persistent role.

SPUI-155 — CONVERSATION-TO-CONVERSATION WORK HANDOFF (OWNER CONFIRMED)
A user can plan a project in an Assistant's Main conversation and hand it to another conversation with the SAME Assistant to implement, or hand off from one organised conversation to another. The receiving conversation can be new or existing. The handoff carries a visible, inspectable and permission-filtered package of the agreed goal, scope, accepted plan/constraints, relevant messages/source references, task/run identity, checkpoints, outputs, remaining work and applicable acceptance criteria, to the extent legitimately authorised. Do NOT move/copy entire private histories indiscriminately or duplicate external side effects. Original source messages remain in their original conversation, with traceable references. The same canonical Assistant identity and existing TaskID/RunIDs persist if continuing the same work; creating a new task requires an explicit genuinely separate objective. Workers must apply changed instructions at safe boundaries. Proposed affordance “Hand off to Conversation” is a useful UI label but exact menu placement/visual presentation remains OPEN for review.

SPUI-169 — UNIVERSAL SPACES STEER / QUEUE WITH PER-SPACE DEFAULT (OWNER CONFIRMED)
ALL applicable conversation-capable Spaces, built-in and user-created, inherit a shared two-mode message submission behaviour for an ongoing response, active agentic run or other applicable execution:
• STEER — send a new instruction to the CURRENT active response/Task/Run to influence work in progress at the next safe supported boundary, preserving accepted work/permissions/checkpoints and reporting whether it was received or actually applied;
• QUEUE — retain the new message/instruction as a genuine QUEUED follow-up for the conversation/eligible run, to be consumed after the current activity reaches its appropriate completion/safe boundary, without interrupting the active response or falsely claiming it has already been processed.
A USER-CONFIGURABLE PREFERRED SEND ACTION MUST exist INDEPENDENTLY FOR EACH SPACE. The preferred value (Steer or Queue) determines that Space's normal send/Enter behaviour during an eligible ongoing response/run, rather than being one global default for every Space. This preference persists across navigation, app restarts and supported user/account synchronisation under existing Home/Spaces preference ownership and Space Overrides > User Preferences > Default precedence; do not alter unrelated preferences or let one Space override another. Expose the selected action visibly and let users switch between Steer/Queue within the composer when applicable. The Research Space preferred/default behaviour at the current owner confirmation is STEER during active research. For other Spaces, the precise initial fallback choice when no preference exists remains OPEN for owner review; do not silently assert one global default. SPUI-174 — REQUIRED VERSUS PREFERRED CONSTRAINTS (OWNER CONFIRMED)
Every applicable user search criterion/filter can be explicitly marked REQUIRED or PREFERRED, with effective semantics visible and user-editable. The user can declare them in a prompt or select/change them directly in the filter interface; the assistant can interpret natural language, but must not silently harden a preference into a mandatory criterion, or overlook an explicit hard constraint. Examples: “black hairdryer under £100, preferably next-day delivery” means black + price cap REQUIRED and next-day delivery PREFERRED unless the user revises them. A product satisfying all VERIFIED/KNOWN REQUIRED conditions may be a DIRECT RESULT even if it lacks a preferred property; preferred matches influence ranking/explanations rather than mandatory eligibility. If available evidence does not establish a mandatory feature, never claim the product definitively meets it. Changing Required/Preferred must immediately and honestly recompute categorisation, rankings, match explanations and where relevant product/offer counts from actual data.

SPUI-175 — THREE PRIMARY RESULT CATEGORIES (OWNER CONFIRMED)
At the top level of the product-results workspace the three named sections/tabs are EXACTLY: “Direct Results” | “Similar Results” | “Other”.
DIRECT RESULTS: products whose documented, currently supported attributes meet all current REQUIRED constraints, whether or not every PREFERRED feature is present. The product must be real and its claimed specifications, delivery and offer data grounded; do not pad this tab with unverified supposedly exact matches.
SIMILAR RESULTS: relevant alternatives meeting some, but not all, required criteria, with clear per-product disclosure of the specific missing/mismatched REQUIRED properties, unknown fields, and useful matching features. Example: a blue hairdryer with a disinfection feature when the user requested black; it belongs here if black is Required. If black is only Preferred, the same blue hairdryer may qualify as Direct, with its preference shortfall explained.
OTHER: carefully relevant recommendations based on the present shopping intent PLUS legitimate, permission-eligible history/preferences/context. Example: after previous discussion of a broken fridge, smart-fridge results may be contextually relevant when currently shopping for smart toasters; unrelated gloves/shoes must NOT surface merely because they were also mentioned historically. Other must not masquerade as fulfilment of required search constraints, exploit sensitive context, or expose unauthorised memories. Keep the explanation for why a related suggestion appeared inspectable and provide appropriate normal memory/personalisation controls under existing Home/Dulche policy. “Other” is a relevance-gated discovery surface, not indiscriminate advertising, and must still meet source-truthfulness rules.
All three tabs use actual product records and user/session requirements; switching tabs must not reset filters or lose the conversation. Where no results qualify, show an honest empty state and offer appropriate refinements rather than fabricate matches.

SPUI-183 — USER MESSAGE ACTIONS AND NONDESTRUCTIVE HISTORY
DEFAULT USER COPY copies only that selected user message. EDIT offers three visibly distinct operations: (1) “Replace messages below”: change the message and supersede downstream messages in the CURRENT ACTIVE VIEW/BRANCH while preserving their recoverable historical branch/event records and actual external side effects; (2) “Update context and new messages only”: create a versioned, prospective correction used for subsequent model context/replies WITHOUT retroactively changing existing responses; (3) “Edit in branch”: construct a new, versioned conversation branch at the selected point while retaining the original branch and provenance. DELETE offers “Delete message” and “Delete message and response”; deletion from the visible active conversation is not assumed to destroy audit, approval or external action history, and genuine data erasure must follow canonical authorised storage/retention/privacy lifecycle. For responses with multiple alternatives, deletion targets must be explicit. Never promise that rewriting history automatically reverses purchases, publishes, tool calls or files. Preserve correct MessageID/BranchID/TaskID links, conflict handling, undo/recoverability where valid, notifications to affected in-flight workers and user-visible scope.

SPUI-188 — PEER REVIEW PLUGIN: MODES, MODEL CHOICE AND SCHEDULE
Add configurable “Peer Review” Plugin using the EXISTING Dulche agentic/Task/Run/Autoreview/verification services. Two distinct behaviours:
SINGLE-THREAD: after a bounded agentic pass, one or more independently configured reviewer models check output against the original objective, constraints, accepted plan, tests, artifacts and evidence for mistakes, deviations, stale tests, security/permission or integration failures. May use another configured model OR an isolated fresh instance of the same model with separate appropriate context; never fabricate independence or copy private hidden reasoning/credentials.
PERSISTENT: review ongoing work on meaningful CHECKPOINTS and/or roughly every 20–30 minutes at a natural safe break; an evidence-based reviewer can adapt the interval (e.g. every 1–2 hours after sustained compliance or around every 5 minutes during repeated mistakes/repair), respecting checkpoints, actual activity, model cost, worker responsiveness and limits. The worker and reviewer MAY discuss disputed findings and request evidence, but the reviewer MUST independently inspect observable work, requirements and tests rather than simply accept a worker's assertion. Review decisions are versioned, inspectable and linked to correct TaskIDs/RunIDs; no duplicate alternate task store or invented automatic “PASS”.
Peer Review settings MUST expose “Models” with user-selectable configured reviewers and “+ Add Model”; default illustrated selection “Qwen 3.8 27B” is an EXAMPLE, not a mandate to install/claim availability. Expose “Max Review Time” as a user-configurable percentage of PRODUCTIVE ACTIVE TASK WORKING TIME, with the owner's selected default example of 25%. The meaning and enforcement are NOW RESOLVED in SPUI-200: the aggregate active peer-review duration cannot exceed that percentage of genuine productive task execution time. This is not a wall-clock fraction, token budget or 25% of combined work plus reviews. Mandatory safety, human approval and independent acceptance gates remain binding.

SPUI-189 — PEER REVIEW POWERS, APPROVAL AND INDEPENDENT ACCEPTANCE
The owner-specified configurable DELEGATED POWERS and proposed initial checkbox states are:
CHECKED: Pause, Resume, and Restart Work; Perform Interventionary Work (e.g. correcting a detected code mistake).
UNCHECKED: Restart Worker; Reset Worker Context; Change Worker Model; Stop/Quarantine Workers.
Additional CHECKED option: “Require All Risky Worker Tool calls to be Approved by a Peer”.
Each enabled capability requires real, explicit Home/Dulche delegated authority, scope and target restrictions, event audit, revocation and recovery. Distinguish restarting WORK from terminating/replacing a WORKER, and NEVER lose valid approved checkpoints, task identity or accepted outputs. Interventionary work follows normal source ownership, diff, tests, permission and conflict rules. Changing a worker model or context respects capability, model route/privacy, recoverability, memory boundaries and user's current authorisation. Quarantine prevents further potentially harmful actions under a documented recoverable policy; it does not stealthily destroy work or erase evidence.
When “Require All Risky Worker Tool calls to be Approved by a Peer” is ON, actual policy-classified risky calls require independent reviewer approval BEFORE executing; if the reviewer is unavailable, HOLD just the gated action while permitting independent safe work where valid. No model peer's approval EVER replaces mandatory human consent, administrator policy or canonical safety enforcement. Failed reviewer checks, unverified output and wrong model interpretations remain visible; a peer's reported PASS alone does not establish VERIFIED. Relevant approval evidence, reviewer identity, task revision, rationale and risk classification are inspectable. The reviewer cannot grant itself unapproved powers or weaken tests to finish.

Daily user-scoped rotation of a DERIVED DATA-ACCESS/ENVELOPE KEY or equivalent sound cryptographic design MAY fulfil the owner's desired daily refreshed unique key, with secure retention of the ability to decrypt legitimately retained older records; never rotate destructively or imply every user gets the same secret.

Expose a purpose-built, scoped Dulche Context Broker, accessible through an authenticated dedicated MCP/interface where appropriate. Opaque capability/handle references may be passed where safe, but must not be reusable bearer secrets the model can leak. Protect integrity, logging/redaction, revocation, key-loss recovery and encryption-state migration.

SPUI-196 — DULCHE BUILT-IN SAFETY BLOCK: CONTEXTUAL LOW-OVERHEAD CHECKS
Build an efficient, integrated safety layer for Dulche that does not normally stall harmless generation. A lightweight CPU-friendly streaming detector MAY flag risk signals/patterns, but simple blacklisted WORDS, WORD PAIRS or short topic lists are NOT sole evidence of policy violation. Words with common benign legal, educational, historical, fictional or technical uses must receive CONTEXTUAL classification rather than automatic refusal. Use layered policy: concise consistent baseline guidance to models (not a pretend exhaustive few-hundred-token “security wall”); streamed output checks; contextual risk assessment; independent pre-execution tool-call/app/permission/scope checks; and where uncertainty or high risk warrants, isolated peer-model or authorised human review. Assessment should consider user intent, whether a request is actually prohibited, severity, legitimate educational/helpful exceptions, and the true capabilities of the chosen model/tool. A reviewer may run asynchronously AFTER low-risk material where safe; genuinely high-risk material/tool actions can be HELD before output or execution. Display “Checking Compliance” only when an actual review/pause occurs, with truthful state rather than cosmetic delay. Response latency should be optimised and measured rather than promising zero overhead or relying exclusively on text scanning. No arbitrary cloud disclosure of private content to a review provider outside current permission/locality policy.

Resolve SPUI-188 and the former SPUI-199 open question definitively. “Max Review Time: 25% of Task” means: for every X minutes of ACTUAL PRODUCTIVE TASK EXECUTION WORK, the allowed cumulative time spent by peer-review models is at most 25% × X (or the user-selected configured percentage). At 4 hours productive work, up to 1 hour aggregate review work is allowed. Formal budget equation: R <= (p/100) × W, where W is real productive active task-work duration EXCLUDING reviewer execution, waiting, pausing, approvals, idle time or merely keeping a host connected; R is AGGREGATE REAL ACTIVE PEER-REVIEW EXECUTION DURATION across all reviewer instances, not an independent allowance per reviewer. Review after each checkpoint or adaptive intervals draws from the SAME budget, including deliberation with workers, reinspection and intervention-related review activity; reviewers must not hide their time in the worker counter or create additional independent caps. Active overlapping productive worker intervals use an honest canonical task clock rather than summing simultaneous worker durations to artificially inflate W; track actual review-resource cost separately when parallel reviewers operate.
Show used/allowed peer-review time and remaining headroom clearly, update using actual measured Task/Run events, and allow the user to change the percentage subject to policy/resource caps and explicit authorisation. This percentage is an overhead LIMIT, NOT a quota peer review must consume and NOT a guarantee of review completeness. If the remaining budget is exhausted, do not silently keep spending reviewer time, pretend a review was performed or mark acceptance VERIFIED. Necessary policy/permission/independent-review gates still apply: suspend only the risky gated action, continue safe independent work where valid, or seek explicit authorised adjustment/review capacity. Validate worker clock, reviewers with different model backends, parallel reviews, pause/restart/reconnection and partial review recovery without duplicate accounting. STUDY-UI-217 — My Progress retains the existing RED / AMBER / GREEN topic tracker while making a FOURTH explicit unassessed state visible: NOT ASSESSED (neutral/no reliable evidence); NEEDS WORK (red, demonstrated difficulty); DEVELOPING (amber, some success but inconsistent or insufficient evidence); CONFIDENT (green, repeated positive evidence across sufficiently meaningful attempts/reviews). Red/amber/green must be backed by recorded events/rules, not user interface impression, AI flattering the learner, material opens or arbitrary confidence claims. Confidence and performance should both be inspectable.

Preserve all existing donor-functionality, security, accessibility, reliability and independent acceptance requirements. It specifies scalable content handling; it does not claim literally infinite resources.

original_text: SCALE-001 — NO ARBITRARY SIZE CEILINGS. First-party 9to1-native documents/projects MUST NOT impose fixed global character, word, page, slide, block, object or file-byte caps just to simplify UI rendering, opening or saving. Allow practical growth subject to available disk/remote quota, supported format, filesystem/address-space and security limits. Avoid hard-coded application-wide caps when scalable indexing, streaming or chunking can address the bottleneck. Disclose every real limiting factor and prevent silent truncation.

original_text: SCALE-002 — USER-FACING PRIORITY. Pointer/keyboard input, caret, selection, active-region edits, scroll, drag and undo/redo are highest-priority work. Near-viewport prefetched rendering and user-requested navigation are next. Unrelated distant pagination/layout, content analysis, indexing, thumbnails, previews and sync are lower priority. Use responsive scheduling, cancellation, backpressure and background work; off-screen processing MUST NOT be a prerequisite for normal editing in the visible region.

original_text: SCALE-003 — CANONICAL STATE SEPARATE FROM VIEW. The persisted editable model, identities, relationships, undo/operation history and search semantics MUST be independent of materialised UI nodes, caches, page thumbnails or rendered slides. Never equate unrendered with nonexistent. Unloaded content remains consistent, accessible, searchable, exportable and editable after hydration, with correct reopen behaviour.

original_text: SCALE-004 — VIRTUALISED / STREAMED RENDERING. Render the visible pages/slides/tiles/cells/blocks/nodes/tracks plus a bounded adaptive buffer. Use region-based culling, placeholder sizing, lazy hydration, thumbnail/preview caching and eviction; do not instantiate the entire artifact's UI tree. Adapt prefetch to scrolling speed, device resources and expected jumps. Maintain memory budgets and gracefully reduce preview fidelity or buffer size under pressure, not document fidelity.

original_text: SCALE-005 — INCREMENTAL CALCULATION. Edit the current region immediately and invalidate only affected dependent layout/index/cache ranges. Reflow, paginate, rebuild derived views and thumbnails progressively with chunk or section indexes, layout checkpoints, dependency-aware invalidation and version/generation checks so stale computations cannot overwrite newer edits. Show provisional page counts or progress honestly until exact values are known; eventual output must be correct.

original_text: SCALE-006 — INDEXED NAVIGATION. Deep jumps, headings/outline, bookmarks, slide navigator, find/replace and selection across distant or unloaded regions use stable content IDs and persisted/incremental indexes. Do not require scanning/rendering all earlier pages to find a position. Show genuine progress for expensive uncached navigation instead of freezing or reporting guessed locations as certain.

original_text: SCALE-007 — CHUNKED PERSISTENCE. Prefer addressable chunks/objects, changed-range delta/operation saves, transactional/atomic commit, versioning, integrity checks, crash-safe recovery and bounded undo/snapshot retention. Autosave MUST NOT repeatedly serialise the whole large artifact per keystroke. Detect and resolve concurrent mutations rather than silently overwriting user content; safely clean orphaned chunks, temp files and caches.

original_text: SCALE-008 — STREAMING IMPORT, EXPORT AND MEDIA. Read/write/transfer large data incrementally; support resuming and cancelling long work with truthful job status and error recovery. Avoid full-file memory duplication wherever possible. Do not claim complete export until all required chunks, relationships and media have been validated and committed. Where a third-party format/provider has a genuine size/count limit, state it and offer a truthful native-format or partitioned workflow, never a fake success.

original_text: SCALE-009 — FILES AND CLOUD. Files MUST support stable asset identity, metadata indexing, byte-range or chunk-aware operations, integrity-verified resumable uploads/downloads, revisions, permissions, transactional commits and recovery. External cloud/storage quotas and device capacity may constrain actual sizes, but MUST be made transparent; no disguised universal file-size cap. Preserve privacy, secure storage and offline access according to the rest of V2.

original_text: SCALE-010 — SAFETY / RELIABILITY. Preserve disk-space margins, bounded caches and memory/CPU/VRAM budgets. Implement backpressure, malicious-file and decompression-bomb protection, limits for untrusted parser operations and safe failure handling. On insufficient resources, report the resource constraint, preserve changes, allow a safe retry/resume or lower preview resolution; never corrupt or silently discard content. Security constraints are valid even when they require rejecting malicious inputs.

original_text: SCALE-011 — CROSS-DEVICE / CROSS-APP. The native Windows/Linux and browser versions must share the same canonical scalable-content semantics, with truthful platform-specific limits. Embedded documents/slides/boards, shared search, AI features and cross-app conversion must not force whole-project eager loading. Maintain accessibility and keyboard navigation across virtualised regions. No downgraded web implementation may falsely display a truncated artifact as complete.

original_text: WRITE-SCALE-201 — LONG DOCUMENTS. Write MUST support content well beyond conventional single-document character limits using visible/adjacent page rendering, section-based hydration, incremental line wrapping and pagination, indexed find/replace, accessible semantic headings, deep jumps, and correct undo/redo. Inserting text near page 1 of a very long document must not synchronously reflow every distant page. Preserve authentic document layout/export correctness once background work completes.

original_text: PRESENT-SCALE-201 — VERY LARGE DECKS. Present MUST lazily create selected-slide and near-slide surfaces, virtualise slide lists/thumbnails, incrementally update slide order/section indexes, retain persistent SlideIDs and NotesIDs, and load embedded media on demand. Inserting/reordering a slide cannot require reconstructing all slide UI. Playback and export must process every applicable slide accurately via bounded batches or truthful progress. No arbitrary native slide-count or file-byte ceiling.

All other applicable apps use corresponding index/stream/cull methods while retaining their real workflows.

original_text: SCALE-AC-201 — TESTING AND MEASUREMENT. Independent acceptance MUST include representative small/medium/large and stress real-artifact tests across supported platforms. Example stress targets: >=1,000 pages in Write, >=10,000 slides in Present where reasonable on test hardware, sizeable binary files, nested/embedded artifacts and large tables/boards. Capture cold/warm load, input and scroll latency, frame times, memory/VRAM/disk consumption, deep-jump latency, edits near start/end, asynchronous reflow, incremental save, recovery after interruption, search across unloaded regions, reopen and full export/import integrity. Define platform/device-specific budgets and report actual results; no fake data, hidden drops or assertions based only on successful startup.

Existing application-specific verification and donor-parity gates remain in force.
